components.name: Button
components.description: Triggers an action or event.
components.markdown:
# Button Triggers an action or event. ## Examples ### Default The default button uses `tone="neutral"` and `appearance="subtle"`. ```tsx import { Button } from '@var-ui/react'; ``` ```astro --- import { Button } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- ``` ```html ``` ### Variants Use `tone` and `appearance` to control color and surface treatment — the same vocabulary as `Badge`, `Alert`, and `Banner`. - **tone** — `neutral`, `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info` - **appearance** — `filled`, `outline`, `subtle`, `ghost` Each row below is one appearance; each button in the row is a different tone. ```tsx import { Button, HStack, VStack } from '@var-ui/react'; const tones = ['neutral', 'accent', 'success', 'warning', 'danger', 'info'] as const; const appearances = ['filled', 'outline', 'subtle', 'ghost'] as const; {appearances.map((appearance) => ( {tones.map((tone) => ( ))} ))} ``` ```astro --- import { Button, HStack, VStack } from '@var-ui/astro'; const tones = ['neutral', 'accent', 'success', 'warning', 'danger', 'info'] as const; const appearances = ['filled', 'outline', 'subtle', 'ghost'] as const; --- {appearances.map((appearance) => ( {tones.map((tone) => ( ))} ))} ``` ```html
``` ### Disabled Pass `isDisabled` to remove the button from the tab order and block press events. ```tsx import { Button, HStack } from '@var-ui/react'; ``` ```astro --- import { Button, HStack } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- ``` ```html
``` ## HTML Set `data-tone` and `data-appearance` on a `.var-ui-button` element (plus `data-size` and `data-layout` when needed). In TypeScript, use `button({ tone, appearance })` from `@var-ui/core`. ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | className | string \| undefined | no | | | | ref | Ref \| undefined | no | | Ref to the underlying `

props.name: ref

props.name: aria-controls
props.description:
Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current
element.

props.name: aria-current
props.description:
Indicates whether this element represents the current item within a container or set of related
elements.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

props.name: aria-details
props.description:
Identifies the element (or elements) that provide a detailed, extended description for the
object.

props.name: aria-disabled
props.description: Indicates whether the element is disabled to users of assistive technology.

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description:
Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded
or collapsed.

props.name: aria-haspopup
props.description:
Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that
can be triggered by an element.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: autoFocus
props.description: Whether the element should receive focus on render.

props.name: children
props.description:
The children of the component. A function may be provided to alter the children based on
component state.

props.name: excludeFromTabOrder
props.description:
Whether to exclude the element from the sequential tab order. If true,
the element will not be focusable via the keyboard by tabbing. This should
be avoided except in rare scenarios where an alternative means of accessing
the element or its functionality via the keyboard is available.

props.name: form
props.description:
The `<form>` element to associate the button with.
The value of this attribute must be the id of a `<form>` in the same document.
See [MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Elements/button#form).

props.name: formAction
props.description:
The URL that processes the information submitted by the button.
Overrides the action attribute of the button's form owner.

props.name: formEncType
props.description: Indicates how to encode the form data that is submitted.

props.name: formMethod
props.description: Indicates the HTTP method used to submit the form.

props.name: formNoValidate
props.description: Indicates that the form is not to be validated when it is submitted.

props.name: formTarget
props.description: Overrides the target attribute of the button's form owner.

props.name: id
props.description:
The element's unique identifier. See
[MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/id).

props.name: isDisabled
props.description: Whether the button is disabled.

props.name: isPending
props.description:
Whether the button is in a pending state. This disables press and hover events
while retaining focusability, and announces the pending state to screen readers.

props.name: name
props.description: Submitted as a pair with the button's value as part of the form data.

props.name: onBlur
props.description: Handler that is called when the element loses focus.

props.name: onClick
props.description:
**Not recommended – use `onPress` instead.** `onClick` is an alias for `onPress`
provided for compatibility with other libraries. `onPress` provides
additional event details for non-mouse interactions.

props.name: onFocus
props.description: Handler that is called when the element receives focus.

props.name: onFocusChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the element's focus status changes.

props.name: onHoverChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the hover state changes.

props.name: onHoverEnd
props.description: Handler that is called when a hover interaction ends.

props.name: onHoverStart
props.description: Handler that is called when a hover interaction starts.

props.name: onKeyDown
props.description: Handler that is called when a key is pressed.

props.name: onKeyUp
props.description: Handler that is called when a key is released.

props.name: onPress
props.description: Handler that is called when the press is released over the target.

props.name: onPressChange
props.description: Handler that is called when the press state changes.

props.name: onPressEnd
props.description:
Handler that is called when a press interaction ends, either
over the target or when the pointer leaves the target.

props.name: onPressStart
props.description: Handler that is called when a press interaction starts.

props.name: onPressUp
props.description:
Handler that is called when a press is released over the target, regardless of
whether it started on the target or not.

props.name: preventFocusOnPress
props.description:
Whether to prevent focus from moving to the button when pressing it.

Caution, this can make the button inaccessible and should only be used when alternative
keyboard interaction is provided, such as ComboBox's MenuTrigger or a NumberField's
increment/decrement control.

props.name: render
props.description:
Overrides the default DOM element with a custom render function.
This allows rendering existing components with built-in styles and behaviors
such as router links, animation libraries, and pre-styled components.

Requirements:

- You must render the expected element type (e.g. if `<button>` is expected, you cannot render an
  `<a>`).
- Only a single root DOM element can be rendered (no fragments).
- You must pass through props and ref to the underlying DOM element, merging with your own prop
  as appropriate.

props.name: slot
props.description:
A slot name for the component. Slots allow the component to receive props from a parent
component. An explicit `null` value indicates that the local props completely override all
props received from a parent.

props.name: style
props.description:
The inline [style](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLElement/style) for the
element. A function may be provided to compute the style based on component state.

props.name: type
props.description: The behavior of the button when used in an HTML form.

props.name: value
props.description: The value associated with the button's name when it's submitted with the form data.

components.name: IconButton
components.description: Icon-only button for compact toolbars and controls.
components.markdown:
# IconButton

Icon-only button for compact toolbars and controls. Shares `tone` / `appearance` / `size` with `Button`, and always uses `layout="icon"`. Pair with `ButtonGroup` or `Toolbar` for dense action rows.

## Examples

### Default

Pass a semantic `name` from the icon registry and a required `aria-label` — the control has no visible text.

```tsx
import { IconButton } from '@var-ui/react';

<IconButton name="close" aria-label="Close" />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Sizes

Use `size` (`sm` / `md` / `lg`) with the same `tone` and `appearance` props as `Button`.

```tsx
import { HStack, IconButton, VStack } from '@var-ui/react';

<VStack gap="lg">
  <HStack gap="sm">
    <IconButton name="search" aria-label="Search small" size="sm" />
    <IconButton name="search" aria-label="Search medium" size="md" />
    <IconButton name="search" aria-label="Search large" size="lg" />
  </HStack>
  <HStack gap="sm">
    <IconButton name="close" aria-label="Close" />
    <IconButton name="search" aria-label="Search" tone="accent" appearance="filled" />
    <IconButton name="menu" aria-label="Menu" tone="accent" appearance="ghost" />
    <IconButton name="close" aria-label="Delete" tone="danger" appearance="filled" />
  </HStack>
</VStack>
```


```html

```

components.markdown:
# ButtonGroup

Groups related buttons into a connected control with shared borders. Works with `Button`, `IconButton`, and mixes of both.

## Examples

### Default

Wrap adjacent `Button`s so they render as one segmented strip.

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup } from '@var-ui/react';

<ButtonGroup>
  <Button>One</Button>
  <Button>Two</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

### With icons

Mix `IconButton` and `Button` children when the group needs compact icon actions alongside a labeled control.

```tsx
import { Button, ButtonGroup, IconButton } from '@var-ui/react';

<ButtonGroup>
  <IconButton name="search" aria-label="Search" />
  <IconButton name="copy" aria-label="Copy" />
  <Button>More</Button>
</ButtonGroup>
```

components.markdown:
# CopyButton

Copies a value to the clipboard with visual feedback. Defaults to an icon + label button; pass a render-prop `children` function when you need custom chrome.

## Examples

### Default

Provide the `value` written to the clipboard. Labels default to “Copy” / “Copied” / “Error”.

```tsx
import { CopyButton } from '@var-ui/react';

<CopyButton value="npm i @var-ui/react" />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Custom labels

Override `copyLabel` and `copiedLabel` (and optionally `errorLabel`) for context-specific copy.

```tsx
import { CopyButton } from '@var-ui/react';

<CopyButton
  value="npm i @var-ui/react"
  copyLabel="Copy install command"
  copiedLabel="Copied to clipboard"
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| value | string | yes |  | Text written to the clipboard when copy is triggered. |
| children | ((state: CopyButtonRenderProps) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  | Custom render function; defaults to a styled icon button. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| copiedLabel | string \| undefined | no | Copied | Label for the default button after a successful copy. |
| copyLabel | string \| undefined | no | Copy | Label for the default button when not copied. |
| errorLabel | string \| undefined | no | Error | Label for the default button after a failed copy. |
| timeout | number \| undefined | no | 2000 | Milliseconds before the copied state resets. |

## Accessibility

The default control is a native `button` whose `aria-label` tracks the current state label (`copyLabel`, `copiedLabel`, or `errorLabel`). After a successful copy, the label updates so assistive tech hears the confirmation. Prefer clear verbs over icon-only copy affordances unless you supply an explicit render-prop with its own accessible name.

<CopyButton
  value="npm i @var-ui/react"
  copyLabel="Copy install command"
  copiedLabel="Copied to clipboard"
/>

# ToggleButton

Pressable toggle that stays selected until pressed again. Use for formatting tools, filters, and other on/off actions that are not mutually exclusive (use `SegmentedControl` for exclusive choices).

## Examples

### Default

Uncontrolled toggles start unselected; press to flip `aria-pressed`.

```tsx
import { ToggleButton } from '@var-ui/react';

<ToggleButton>Bold</ToggleButton>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Pressed state

Use `defaultSelected` for an initially pressed uncontrolled toggle, or `isSelected` + `onChange` for controlled selection.

```tsx
import { HStack, ToggleButton } from '@var-ui/react';
import { useState } from 'react';

const [italic, setItalic] = useState(true);

<HStack gap="sm">
  <ToggleButton defaultSelected>Bold</ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton isSelected={italic} onChange={setItalic}>
    Italic
  </ToggleButton>
  <ToggleButton>Underline</ToggleButton>
</HStack>
```

components.markdown:
# SegmentedControl

Segmented toggle group for mutually exclusive options. Built on React Aria `ToggleButtonGroup` with an animated indicator. Prefer this over a row of standalone `ToggleButton`s when only one choice should be active.

## Examples

### Default

Pass `options` as `{ id, label }` and seed selection with `defaultSelectedKeys`.

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from '@var-ui/react';

<SegmentedControl
  selectionMode="single"
  defaultSelectedKeys={['list']}
  options={[
    { id: 'list', label: 'List' },
    { id: 'grid', label: 'Grid' },
  ]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Controlled selection

Drive selection with `selectedKeys` and `onSelectionChange` when the active segment must sync with app state.

```tsx
import { SegmentedControl } from '@var-ui/react';
import { useState } from 'react';
import type { Selection } from 'react-aria-components';

const [selectedKeys, setSelectedKeys] = useState<Selection>(new Set(['list']));

<SegmentedControl
  selectionMode="single"
  selectedKeys={selectedKeys}
  onSelectionChange={setSelectedKeys}
  options={[
    { id: 'list', label: 'List' },
    { id: 'grid', label: 'Grid' },
    { id: 'board', label: 'Board' },
  ]}
/>
```

# ColorModeToggle

Switch between light, dark, and optional system color modes. Built on `SegmentedControl`. Inside `DesignSystemProvider` it reads context; otherwise pass both `colorMode` and `onColorModeChange`.

## Examples

### Default

Icon-only segments for light and dark. Controlled demos pass `colorMode` / `onColorModeChange`.

```tsx
import { ColorModeToggle } from '@var-ui/react';

<ColorModeToggle colorMode={mode} onColorModeChange={setMode} />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Appearance

Set `appearance` to `labels` or `iconsAndLabels`, and `includeSystem` to add a System segment.

```tsx
import { ColorModeToggle, VStack } from '@var-ui/react';
```

# Menu Action menu namespace. `Menu` is Root for compound menus; use `Menu.FromSections`, `Menu.ContextMenu`, or `Menu.Overflow` for common presets. The trigger child must forward DOM props — there is no `render` prop. Right-click (or the platform context-menu gesture) opens the menu at the pointer. The child must be a DOM element `Pressable` can attach a ref to (e.g. a `div`). ```tsx import { Menu } from '@var-ui/react';

components.name: Toolbar
components.description: Accessible toolbar landmark for grouped controls.
components.markdown:
# Toolbar

Accessible toolbar landmark for grouped controls. Place actions in `startContent`, optional `centerContent`, and `endContent`. A required `label` becomes the toolbar’s `aria-label`.

## Examples

### Default

Start and end slots with buttons — flex layout when center is omitted.

```tsx
import { Button, Toolbar } from '@var-ui/react';

<Toolbar
  label="Document actions"
  startContent={<Button>Bold</Button>}
  endContent={<Button>Share</Button>}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Slots

Provide `startContent`, `centerContent`, and `endContent` together; center forces a grid layout so the middle stays visually centered.

```tsx
import { Button, IconButton, Toolbar } from '@var-ui/react';

<Toolbar
  label="Editor toolbar"
  startContent={
    <>
      <IconButton name="menu" aria-label="Menu" />
      <IconButton name="search" aria-label="Search" />
    </>
  }
  centerContent={<Button>Untitled</Button>}
  endContent={<Button tone="accent" appearance="filled">Share</Button>}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string | yes |  | Accessible label for the toolbar (required — applied as aria-label). |
| centerContent | ReactNode | no |  | Content centered between the start and end slots; forces a grid layout. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  | Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element. |
| endContent | ReactNode | no |  | Content aligned to the end (trailing) edge. |
| orientation | "horizontal" \| "vertical" \| undefined | no | horizontal | Layout axis. |
| size | "lg" \| "md" \| "sm" \| undefined | no | md | Control density. |
| startContent | ReactNode | no |  | Content aligned to the start (leading) edge. |

## Accessibility

Renders `role="toolbar"` with `aria-label` from `label` and `aria-orientation` from `orientation`. Children keep their natural tab order — there is no roving tabindex / arrow-key navigation yet. Ensure each child control has its own accessible name.

components.name: Form
components.description: Native-constraint form that focuses the first invalid field.
components.markdown:
# Form

Native-constraint form that focuses the first invalid field. `Form` is a React `<form>` that runs `checkValidity()` and accepts a server `errors` map keyed by field `name`. A truthy `errors` entry blocks submit; the app owns clearing it — `Form` does not reset `errors` when the control changes.

There is no `@var-ui/astro` Form. Native `required` works in Astro without `Form`; focus-first-invalid is React-only.

## Examples

### Default

Submit with empty required fields to see native messages and focus on the first invalid control.

```tsx
import { Button, Field, Form } from '@var-ui/react';

<Form>
  <Field.Root name="email">
    <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
    <Field.Control>
      <input name="email" type="email" required />
    </Field.Control>
    <Field.Error />
  </Field.Root>
  <Field.Root name="name">
    <Field.Label>Name</Field.Label>
    <Field.Control>
      <input name="name" required />
    </Field.Control>
    <Field.Error />
  </Field.Root>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>
```


## Server errors

Pass an `errors` map keyed by field `name`. A truthy entry blocks submit until the app clears it.

```tsx
<Form errors={{ email: 'Enter a valid email' }}>
  <TextField name="email" label="Email" />
</Form>
```

## Accessibility

Form is React-only; native `required` works in Astro without `Form`. On invalid submit, focus moves to the first `[aria-invalid="true"]` or `:invalid` control.

examples.react:
import { Button, Field, Form } from '@var-ui/react';

<Form>
  <Field.Root name="email">
    <Field.Label>Email</Field.Label>
    <Field.Control>
      <input name="email" type="email" required />
    </Field.Control>
    <Field.Error />
  </Field.Root>
  <Field.Root name="name">
    <Field.Label>Name</Field.Label>
    <Field.Control>
      <input name="name" required />
    </Field.Control>
    <Field.Error />
  </Field.Root>
  <Button type="submit">Save</Button>
</Form>

components.description: Numeric field with increment and decrement steppers.
components.markdown:
# NumberInput

Numeric field with increment and decrement steppers. Built on React Aria `NumberField` with a stepper group for keyboard- and pointer-friendly adjustments. Prefer this over a plain text field when the value must stay numeric.

## Examples

### Default

Pass a `label` and seed with `defaultValue` (or control via `value` / `onChange`).

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<NumberInput label="Quantity" defaultValue={1} />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Bounds and step

Clamp the range with `minValue` / `maxValue` and set `step` for how far each stepper click (or arrow key) moves.

```tsx
import { NumberInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<NumberInput
  label="Quantity"
  defaultValue={1}
  minValue={0}
  maxValue={10}
  step={1}
  description="Between 0 and 10"
/>
```

components.markdown:
# PasswordInput

Password field with a show/hide visibility toggle. Masks input by default and flips the native `type` between `password` and `text` when the toggle is pressed.

## Examples

### Default

Provide a `label` (and optional `placeholder`). The visibility button sits inside the field chrome.

```tsx
import { PasswordInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<PasswordInput label="Password" />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Description and error

Use `description` for helper copy and `errorMessage` for validation — setting `errorMessage` marks the field invalid.

```tsx
import { PasswordInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<PasswordInput
  label="Password"
  description="Use at least 8 characters"
  errorMessage="Password is too short"
/>
```

components.description: File picker dropzone with accept and size constraints.
components.markdown:
# FileInput

File picker dropzone with click-to-browse, drag-and-drop, and client-side `accept` / `maxSize` / `maxFiles` validation. Always controlled via `value` and `onChange`.

## Examples

### Default

Pass a required `label`, controlled `value` / `onChange`, and optional `accept` filters.

```tsx
import { FileInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<FileInput label="Upload" value={file} onChange={setFile} accept=".pdf,image/*" />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Multiple files

Set `multiple` so `value` is a `File[]` (or `null` when cleared). Optionally cap the count with `maxFiles`.

```tsx
import { FileInput } from '@var-ui/react';
import { useState } from 'react';

const [files, setFiles] = useState<File[] | null>(null);

<FileInput
  label="Attachments"
  value={files}
  onChange={setFiles}
  multiple
  accept="image/*,.pdf"
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string | yes |  | Visible label rendered above the dropzone. |
| onChange | (files: File \| File[] \| null) => void | yes |  | Called with the new selection, or `null` when cleared. |
| value | File \| File[] \| null | yes |  | Selected file(s); `File[]` when `multiple`, otherwise a single `File` or `null`. |
| accept | string \| undefined | no |  | Comma-separated list of accepted `.ext`, `type/*`, or exact mime types (matches the HTML `accept` attribute). |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  | Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element. |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Helper text shown below the control when there is no error. |
| errorMessage | string \| undefined | no |  | Validation message; when set, takes precedence over internally-derived validation errors. |
| isDisabled | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Disables the dropzone: blocks click, keyboard activation, and drop. |
| maxFiles | number \| undefined | no |  | Maximum number of files accepted when `multiple`. Extra files are rejected. |
| maxSize | number \| undefined | no |  | Maximum size per file, in bytes. Oversized files are rejected. |
| multiple | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Allow selecting/dropping more than one file. |

## Accessibility

The dropzone is a focusable `role="button"` activated with Enter/Space, labelled by the visible field label and described by `description` / error text. The native file input is visually hidden (`aria-hidden`) and opened programmatically. The clear control has an explicit `aria-label` (“Clear …”).

## FileTrigger

`FileTrigger` opens the picker from an existing button. It does not render a dropzone, filename, or field label, and it does not take `value`. `onSelect` receives the chosen files. Choosing the same file again calls `onSelect` again.

```tsx
<FileTrigger accept="image/*" multiple onSelect={(files) => upload(files)}>
  <Button>Choose images</Button>
</FileTrigger>
```

examples.react:
import { FileInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<FileInput label="Upload" value={file} onChange={setFile} accept=".pdf,image/*" />

# InputGroup

Composes bare `InputGroupInput` controls with `InputGroupText` addons for prefixed or suffixed fields. Owns its own field chrome rather than wrapping `TextField` / `NumberInput`.

## Examples

### Default

Place an `InputGroupText` addon before (or after) an `InputGroupInput` inside the group.

```tsx
import { InputGroup, InputGroupInput, InputGroupText } from '@var-ui/react';

<InputGroup label="Price">
  <InputGroupText>$</InputGroupText>
  <InputGroupInput aria-label="Price" />
</InputGroup>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Prefix and suffix addons

Stack multiple `InputGroupText` children on either side of the input so borders join into one control.

```tsx
import { InputGroup, InputGroupInput, InputGroupText } from '@var-ui/react';

<InputGroup label="Website">
  <InputGroupText>https://</InputGroupText>
  <InputGroupInput aria-label="Website" placeholder="example" />
  <InputGroupText>.com</InputGroupText>
</InputGroup>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string | yes |  | Visible label rendered above the group. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Plain `<input>`s (see `InputGroupInput`) and `InputGroupText` addons. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  | Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element. |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Helper text shown below the group when there is no error. |
| errorMessage | string \| undefined | no |  | Validation message; when set, the group is shown in an error state. |
| isDisabled | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Disables the whole group (visually and via `aria-disabled`). |
| size | "lg" \| "md" \| "sm" \| undefined | no | md | Control density inherited by `InputGroupInput` and `InputGroupText`. |

## Accessibility

The outer control uses `role="group"` with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the visible label. Give each `InputGroupInput` its own accessible name (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`) — addon text is visual chrome and is not announced as the input’s name. `errorMessage` is exposed with `role="alert"`.

# CheckboxGroup

Group of checkboxes for multi-select options. Pass `options` as `{ value, label }` pairs; selection is a string array via React Aria `CheckboxGroup`.

## Examples

### Default

Provide a group `label` and `options`. Selection starts empty unless you seed it.

```tsx
import { CheckboxGroup } from '@var-ui/react';

  options={[

    { value: 'billing', label: 'Billing' },

/>
```

```tsx
  defaultValue={['analytics', 'billing']}
```

# Calendar

Standalone month-grid date picker — no popover, no text input. Compose with form chrome elsewhere when you need a labeled field; use `DateInput` when you want segmented typing plus a calendar popover.

## Examples

### Default

Control selection with `value` / `onChange` and `@internationalized/date` (`CalendarDate`). Provide an `aria-label` when there is no visible label.

```tsx
import { CalendarDate } from '@internationalized/date';
import { Calendar } from '@var-ui/react';

<Calendar aria-label="Pick a day" value={value} onChange={setValue} />
```

```astro

```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Minimum date

Pass `minValue` to block dates before a bound. Past (or earlier) days are unavailable while the selected value stays controlled.

```tsx
import { CalendarDate } from '@internationalized/date';
import { Calendar } from '@var-ui/react';

<Calendar
  aria-label="Pick a day"
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
  minValue={new CalendarDate(2026, 8, 1)}
/>
```

# DateInput

Single-date field with segmented text entry (month/day/year) plus a trigger that opens a popover month calendar. Values use `@internationalized/date` (`CalendarDate`).

## Examples

### Default

Pass a `label` and seed with `defaultValue` (or control via `value` / `onChange`).

```tsx
import { CalendarDate } from '@internationalized/date';
import { DateInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<DateInput label="Date" defaultValue={new CalendarDate(2026, 8, 12)} />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Description and error

Use `description` for helper copy and `errorMessage` for validation — setting `errorMessage` marks the field invalid.

```tsx
import { CalendarDate } from '@internationalized/date';
import { DateInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<DateInput
  label="Deadline"
  description="Must be a weekday"
  errorMessage="Pick a weekday"
  defaultValue={new CalendarDate(2026, 8, 15)}
/>
```

components.markdown:
# DateRangeInput

Start/end date field with segmented entry for both sides and a popover range calendar. The controlled `value` is a **range object** `{ start, end }` of `@internationalized/date` values (typically `CalendarDate`), not two separate props.

## Examples

### Default

Seed both ends with `defaultValue={{ start, end }}`.

```tsx
import { CalendarDate } from '@internationalized/date';
import { DateRangeInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<DateRangeInput
  label="Trip"
  defaultValue={{ start: new CalendarDate(2026, 8, 10), end: new CalendarDate(2026, 8, 20) }}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Controlled range

Drive selection with `value` / `onChange`. `onChange` receives the full range (or `null` when cleared).

```tsx
import { CalendarDate } from '@internationalized/date';
import { DateRangeInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<DateRangeInput
  label="Trip"
  value={{ start: new CalendarDate(2026, 8, 10), end: new CalendarDate(2026, 8, 20) }}
  onChange={setValue}
/>
```

components.name: DateTimeInput
components.description: Segmented date and time field with calendar popover.
components.markdown:
# DateTimeInput

Combined date and time field: month/day/year plus hour/minute (and optional seconds / day-period) segments, with a popover calendar for the date portion. Defaults to `granularity="minute"`. Values typically use `CalendarDateTime` from `@internationalized/date`.

## Examples

### Default

Pass a `label` and a `CalendarDateTime` `defaultValue` (or control via `value` / `onChange`).

```tsx
import { CalendarDateTime } from '@internationalized/date';
import { DateTimeInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<DateTimeInput label="Appointment" defaultValue={new CalendarDateTime(2026, 8, 12, 14, 30)} />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Granularity

Set `granularity` to control the smallest editable time unit. `"second"` adds a seconds segment; `"day"` hides time segments entirely.

```tsx
import { CalendarDateTime } from '@internationalized/date';
import { DateTimeInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<DateTimeInput
  label="Appointment"
  defaultValue={new CalendarDateTime(2026, 8, 12, 14, 30, 0)}
  granularity="second"
  description="Includes a seconds segment"
/>
```


components.markdown:
# Tokenizer

Combo-style field that turns selected options into removable tags. Always controlled via `value` / `onChange` — pass the full option objects, not just ids. Selected ids are filtered out of the dropdown so you cannot add the same token twice.

## Examples

### Default

Pass `options` as `{ id, label }[]` and keep selected tokens in React state. Type to filter, pick from the list, or press Backspace on an empty input to remove the last tag.

```tsx
import { Tokenizer } from '@var-ui/react';

<Tokenizer label="Tags" options={options} value={value} onChange={setValue} />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Pre-selected tags

Seed `value` with one or more options to show an existing selection. Pair with `description` or `errorMessage` for field chrome.

```tsx
import { Tokenizer } from '@var-ui/react';
import { useState } from 'react';

const options = [
  { id: 'alpha', label: 'Alpha' },
  { id: 'beta', label: 'Beta' },
  { id: 'gamma', label: 'Gamma' },
  { id: 'delta', label: 'Delta' },
];

const [value, setValue] = useState([options[0], options[2]]);

<Tokenizer
  label="Tags"
  description="Start with a few tokens already selected"
  options={options}
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onChange | (value: TokenizerOption[]) => void | yes |  | Called with the next token array when a token is added or removed. |
| options | TokenizerOption[] | yes |  | Full candidate list; options already present in `value` are excluded from the dropdown. |
| value | TokenizerOption[] | yes |  | Selected tokens (controlled). |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Helper text shown below the group when there is no error. |
| errorMessage | string \| undefined | no |  | Validation message; when set, the field is shown in an error state. |
| isDisabled | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | Field label rendered above the group. |
| placeholder | string \| undefined | no | Add… | Placeholder text shown in the search input when no tokens are selected. |

## Accessibility

Built on React Aria `ComboBox` plus `TagGroup` / `TagList`. The group exposes a labeled remove control on each chip (`Remove {label}`). Keep `label` visible so the field and the selected-tag list share a clear accessible name; use `description` / `errorMessage` for the same helper and validation copy sighted users see. Keyboard: arrow through suggestions, Enter to add, Backspace on an empty input removes the last token.

# MultiSelector

Dropdown that selects multiple options at once. Always controlled via `value` (option ids) and `onChange`. The trigger summarizes the current selection as a comma-separated label list.

## Examples

### Default

Pass `options` as `{ id, label }[]` and seed `value` with the selected ids.

```tsx
import { MultiSelector } from '@var-ui/react';

<MultiSelector label="Teams" options={options} value={value} onChange={setValue} />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Controlled selection

Keep the selected ids in React state and update them from `onChange`. The trigger text and any app UI that depends on the selection stay in sync.

```tsx
import { MultiSelector } from '@var-ui/react';
import { useState } from 'react';

const [value, setValue] = useState(['design', 'ops']);

<MultiSelector
  label="Teams"
  description="Selection stays in React state"
  options={options}
  value={value}
  onChange={setValue}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onChange | (value: string[]) => void | yes |  | Called with the updated selected option ids whenever selection changes. |
| options | MultiSelectorOption[] | yes |  | Options shown in the dropdown listbox. |
| value | string[] | yes |  | Currently selected option ids. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| description | string \| undefined | no |  | Helper text shown below the control when there is no error. |
| errorMessage | string \| undefined | no |  | Validation message; when set, the field is shown in an error state. |
| isDisabled | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| label | string \| undefined | no |  | Visible label rendered above the control. |
| placeholder | string \| undefined | no | Select… | Placeholder text when no value is selected. |

## Accessibility

The trigger is a button labeled by the field `label` plus the current summary text. The popover listbox uses `selectionMode="multiple"` with checkbox affordances on each item. Keep `label` visible, and use `description` / `errorMessage` (the error message is `role="alert"`) so assistive tech gets the same help and validation copy as sighted users.

# ColorInput

Hex text field with a swatch button that opens a full HSV `ColorPicker` popover. Accepts controlled (`value` / `onChange`) or uncontrolled (`defaultValue`) hex strings. Invalid typed hex is ignored until blur, when the field snaps back to the last valid color.

## Examples

### Default

Pass a `label` and seed with `defaultValue` (or control via `value` / `onChange`).

```tsx
import { ColorInput } from '@var-ui/react';

<ColorInput label="Brand" defaultValue="#6366f1" />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Controlled value

Drive the field with `value` and `onChange` when the hex must stay in sync with app state — typing a valid hex or picking from the popover both update the same value.

```tsx
import { ColorInput } from '@var-ui/react';
```

## Accessibility

The text control is a labeled native input (`aria-invalid` when `errorMessage` is set). The swatch is a separate button with `aria-label="Open color picker"` that opens a dialog popover containing the picker. Pass `swatchLabel` to name that button for a specific control (`swatchLabel="Color for Alex"`) when the default is not enough to tell pickers apart. `appearance="swatch"` renders the swatch button and the picker popover, leaving the hex field, visible label, description, and error text on the default `field` appearance. Keep `label` visible on a field, and use `description` / `errorMessage` so assistive tech gets the same help and validation copy as sighted users. A swatch with `name` submits its value through a hidden input.

components.markdown:
# ColorPicker

Full HSV color picker with a saturation panel, hue slider, optional alpha slider, and built-in preset swatches. This page also documents `ColorSwatch` — a compact chip for external palettes wired to the same controlled color.

## Examples

### Default

Seed with `defaultValue` (or control via `value` / `onChange`). A Mantine-compatible preset palette is shown unless you pass `swatches`.

```tsx
import { ColorPicker } from '@var-ui/react';

<ColorPicker defaultValue="#228be6" />
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### With ColorSwatch

Hide the picker’s built-in row (`swatches={[]}`) and drive the color from standalone `ColorSwatch` buttons — useful when presets live outside the picker chrome.

```tsx
import { ColorPicker, ColorSwatch, HStack } from '@var-ui/react';

<ColorPicker value={color} onChange={setColor} swatches={[]} />
<HStack gap="sm">
  <ColorSwatch
    color="#228be6"
    selected={color === '#228be6'}
    aria-label="Blue"
    onClick={() => setColor('#228be6')}
  />
  <ColorSwatch
    color="#40c057"
    selected={color === '#40c057'}
    aria-label="Green"
    onClick={() => setColor('#40c057')}
  />
</HStack>
```

| onChange | ((value: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| swatches | string[] \| undefined | no | Mantine-compatible preset palette | Preset swatches below the sliders. |
| swatchesPerRow | 10 \| 7 \| undefined | no | 7 | Swatches per row. |
| value | string \| undefined | no |  | Controlled hex color (e.g. `#228be6` or `#228be680` with alpha). |
| withAlpha | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show an alpha slider and emit 8-digit hex. |

## Accessibility

Saturation uses `role="application"` with arrow-key nudges; hue and alpha are `role="slider"`. Built-in swatches are a `listbox` of `option`s with `aria-selected`. Standalone `ColorSwatch` is a button with `aria-pressed` when `selected`. Give every external swatch an `aria-label` (the hex or a color name).

components.markdown: # Chip Compact pill-shaped labels. Use `ChipGroup` for coordinated single- or multi-select filter chips, or `Pill` / `onRemove` for removable tags. ## Examples ### Default ```tsx import { Chip, ChipGroup, Pill } from '@var-ui/react'; React Vue remove('docs')}>Documentation ``` ```astro --- import { Chip, Pill } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- Static Documentation ``` ```html React ``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | aria-label | string \| undefined | no | | Accessible name when children are not plain text. | | children | ReactNode | no | | | | className | string \| undefined | no | | | | isDisabled | boolean \| undefined | no | | | | isSelected | boolean \| undefined | no | | Selected state for standalone filter/toggle chips. | | onChange | ((selected: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no | | Called when a standalone toggle chip is pressed. | | onRemove | (() => void) \| undefined | no | | Shows a dismiss control and calls this handler on press. | | removeLabel | string \| undefined | no | Remove | Accessible label for the remove button. | | value | string \| undefined | no | | Selection key when rendered inside `ChipGroup`. | | appearance | "outline" \| "solid" \| "subtle" \| undefined | no | | | | tone | "accent" \| "danger" \| "info" \| "neutral" \| "success" \| "warning" \| undefined | no | | | ## Accessibility Toggle chips render as buttons with `aria-pressed`. # Dialog Modal overlay for focused tasks. `Dialog` is the compound Root (`Dialog.Trigger`, `Dialog.Backdrop`, `Dialog.Popup`, and chrome parts). components.name: AlertDialog
components.description: Confirmation modal for destructive or important actions.
components.markdown:
# AlertDialog

Modal confirmation for important or destructive actions. Uses `role="alertdialog"`, a cancel action, and a confirm action that calls `onConfirm` (cancel / Escape never call `onConfirm`). The default export stays the assembled preset (`title` / `onConfirm` / `triggerLabel`). Compound parts (`AlertDialog.Root`, `AlertDialog.Trigger`, `AlertDialog.Backdrop`, `AlertDialog.Popup`, `AlertDialog.Title`, `AlertDialog.Actions`) are available for custom chrome. The trigger child must forward DOM props — there is no `render` prop.

State attributes, exit animation, and `onOpenChange` details are documented in [Overlay lifecycle](/docs/overlay-lifecycle).

## Examples

### Default

Pass `triggerLabel` for a built-in open button. Set `isDestructive` to style confirm as danger and autofocus Cancel.

```tsx
import { AlertDialog } from '@var-ui/react';

<AlertDialog
  triggerLabel="Delete"
  title="Delete item?"
  description="This cannot be undone."
  confirmLabel="Delete"
  isDestructive
  onConfirm={() => {}}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Confirm pattern

Non-destructive confirms use `tone="accent"` and `appearance="filled"`. Customize `cancelLabel` / `confirmLabel` to match the task.

```tsx
import { AlertDialog } from '@var-ui/react';

<AlertDialog
  triggerLabel="Publish"
  title="Publish post?"
  description="Your draft will become visible to everyone with the link."
  confirmLabel="Publish"
  cancelLabel="Keep editing"
  onConfirm={() => {}}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| onConfirm | () => void | yes |  | Called when the confirm action is pressed. Never called on cancel or Escape dismissal. |
| title | string | yes |  | Dialog heading shown in the modal header. |
| cancelLabel | string \| undefined | no | Cancel | Label for the dismiss action. |
| confirmLabel | string \| undefined | no | Confirm | Label for the confirm action. |
| description | ReactNode | no |  | Supporting copy below the heading. |
| isDestructive | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Renders the confirm action with `tone="danger"` and autofocuses Cancel. |
| isOpen | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Controls the open state. Required when `triggerLabel` is omitted. |
| onOpenChange | OverlayOpenChangeHandler \| undefined | no |  | Called when the open state changes (including Escape/cancel dismissal). |
| portalContainer | Element \| undefined | no |  | Element the modal portals into instead of `document.body`. Needed when a subtree renders under a different theme than the page ambient (the theme's CSS custom properties only cascade to descendants of the themed element). |
| triggerLabel | string \| undefined | no |  | Label on the button that opens the modal. If omitted, use `isOpen`/`onOpenChange` to control it. |

## Accessibility

Renders as an alertdialog with a focus trap. Destructive flows autofocus Cancel so Enter does not immediately confirm. Escape and the cancel button dismiss without calling `onConfirm`. Prefer a clear `title` and short `description` that name the irreversible consequence.

  confirmLabel="Delete"

components.name: Tooltip
components.description: Short hint shown on hover or focus.
components.markdown:
# Tooltip

Brief hint shown on hover or focus of a single trigger. Prefer tooltips for supplemental labels — not essential instructions. `Tooltip` is the compound Root (`Tooltip.Trigger` / `Tooltip.Popup`). The trigger child must forward DOM props — there is no `render` prop. For the previous `content` / `placement` / `delay` API, use the `SimpleTooltip` preset.

State attributes, positioner CSS variables, and `onOpenChange` details are documented in [Overlay lifecycle](/docs/overlay-lifecycle).

## Examples

### Compound parts

Compose Trigger and Popup.

```tsx
import { Button, Tooltip } from '@var-ui/react';

<Tooltip>
  <Tooltip.Trigger>
    <Button>Save</Button>
  </Tooltip.Trigger>
  <Tooltip.Popup>Save changes</Tooltip.Popup>
</Tooltip>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### SimpleTooltip preset

`SimpleTooltip` keeps the assembled 80% case copy-pasteable.

```tsx
import { Button, SimpleTooltip } from '@var-ui/react';

<SimpleTooltip content="Save changes">
  <Button>Save</Button>
</SimpleTooltip>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Placement and delay

Set `placement` relative to the trigger and `delay` (ms) before open. Default delay is 500ms. This demo uses the `SimpleTooltip` preset.

```tsx
import { Button, SimpleTooltip } from '@var-ui/react';

<SimpleTooltip content="Below the trigger" placement="bottom" delay={200}>
  <Button>Bottom · 200ms</Button>
</SimpleTooltip>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| defaultOpen | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| delay | number \| undefined | no | 500 | Delay before the tooltip opens, in milliseconds. |
| isOpen | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| onOpenChange | OverlayOpenChangeHandler \| undefined | no |  |  |
| portalContainer | Element \| undefined | no |  | Element the tooltip portals into instead of `document.body`. Needed when a subtree renders under a different theme than the page ambient. |

## Accessibility

Tooltips appear on hover and keyboard focus. Keep copy short; do not put interactive content in a tooltip (use `HoverCard` or `Popover` instead). The trigger must already have an accessible name — tooltips supplement, they do not replace labels.

components.name: HoverCard
components.description: Rich preview card shown on hover or focus.
components.markdown:
# HoverCard Rich preview shown on hover or focus. Unlike `Tooltip`, content may include interactive elements (links). Open/close delays are independent (`openDelay` / `closeDelay`). `HoverCard` stays the assembled preset (`trigger` / `title` / children). Compound parts (`HoverCard.Root`, `HoverCard.Trigger`, `HoverCard.Popup`, `HoverCard.Title`, `HoverCard.Content`) are available for custom chrome. The trigger child must forward DOM props — there is no `render` prop. State attributes, positioner CSS variables, and `onOpenChange` details are documented in [Overlay lifecycle](/docs/overlay-lifecycle). ## Examples ### Default Wrap a focusable `trigger` (often a `Link`) and pass preview children. ```tsx import { HoverCard, Link } from '@var-ui/react'; Ada Lovelace} title="Ada Lovelace">

Mathematician and early computing pioneer.

 ``` ```astro ``` ```html ``` ### Rich content Add a `title` plus denser body copy or links for profile / entity previews. ```tsx import { HoverCard, Link, Text } from '@var-ui/react'; @ada} title="Ada Lovelace"> Mathematician and early computing pioneer. View profile ``` ```astro ``` ```html ``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | trigger | ReactElement \| string> | yes | | Single focusable trigger element (e.g. a link or avatar). | | children | ReactNode | no | | Rich preview content — may contain interactive elements such as links. | | closeDelay | number \| undefined | no | 300 | Delay before the card closes after the pointer/focus leaves, in milliseconds. | | openDelay | number \| undefined | no | 700 | Delay before the card opens on hover/focus, in milliseconds. | | placement | Placement \| undefined | no | top | Preferred placement relative to the trigger. | | portalContainer | Element \| undefined | no | | Element the card portals into instead of `document.body`. Needed when a subtree renders under a different theme than the page ambient. | | title | ReactNode | no | | Optional heading shown at the top of the card. | ## Accessibility Opens on hover and focus without trapping focus, so users can move into the card to activate links. Prefer generous hit targets on the trigger. For click-only panels use `Popover`.

import { HoverCard, Link } from '@var-ui/react'; Ada Lovelace} title="Ada Lovelace">

Mathematician and early computing pioneer.

import { HoverCard, Link, Text } from '@var-ui/react';

<HoverCard trigger={<Link href="/u/ada">@ada</Link>} title="Ada Lovelace">
  <Text size="sm" tone="secondary">
    Mathematician and early computing pioneer.
  </Text>
  <Link href="/u/ada">View profile</Link>
</HoverCard>

components.markdown:
# CommandPalette ⌘K-style searchable command overlay. You own `isOpen` / `onOpenChange` and typically close inside `onAction`. Items match on `title`, `meta`, and optional `keywords`. The panel uses overlay presence attributes (`data-open`, `data-starting-style`, `data-ending-style`); see [Overlay lifecycle](/docs/overlay-lifecycle). `onOpenChange` is still `(open: boolean)`. ## Examples ### Default Open from a button (demos disable the global hotkey so pages stay calm). ```tsx import { CommandPalette } from '@var-ui/react'; setOpen(false)} /> ``` ```astro --- import { CommandPalette } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- ``` ```html
…
``` ### Grouped results via meta Use `meta` (and `keywords`) so related commands are scannable and searchable even when titles are short. ```tsx import { Button, CommandPalette } from '@var-ui/react'; import { useState } from 'react'; const [open, setOpen] = useState(false); setOpen(false)} /> ``` ```astro ``` ```html ``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | items | CommandPaletteItem[] | yes | | Commands shown in the results list. | | onAction | (id: string) => void | yes | | Called with the selected item's `id` on Enter/click; the palette does not close itself. | | emptyLabel | string \| undefined | no | 'No results' | Message shown when no items match the query. | | filter | ((item: CommandPaletteItem, query: string) => boolean) \| undefined | no | | Overrides the default case-insensitive title/meta/keywords match. | | hotkey | boolean \| undefined | no | true | Toggles open state on ⌘K / Ctrl+K. | | isOpen | boolean \| undefined | no | | Controls the open state. | | onOpenChange | ((open: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no | | Called when the open state changes (Escape, backdrop click, hotkey, or item selection). | | placeholder | string \| undefined | no | 'Search…' | Input placeholder. | | portalContainer | Element \| undefined | no | | Element the dialog renders into instead of its React parent. Needed when a subtree renders under a different theme than the page ambient (the theme's CSS custom properties only cascade to descendants of the themed element). | ## Accessibility When open, focus moves to the search field; arrow keys move through results, Enter activates, Escape closes. Provide clear `title` text — `meta` is secondary. The default hotkey is ⌘K / Ctrl+K (`hotkey`); disable it in embedded demos if it would fight the host page.

/>

# Accordion Stacked disclosure panels built on React Aria `DisclosureGroup`. Use the compound `Accordion.Item`, `Accordion.Trigger`, and `Accordion.Panel` API for FAQ and settings layouts. For a single standalone panel, use [`Collapsible`](/components/collapsible). ## Examples ### Default ```tsx import { Accordion } from '@var-ui/react'; Billing … Shipping … ``` ```astro --- import { Accordion, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger, AccordionPanel, } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- Billing … ``` ```html
…
``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | children | ReactNode | no | | | | className | string \| undefined | no | | | | collapsible | boolean \| undefined | no | true | When `type` is `single`, allow closing every panel. | | defaultExpandedKeys | Iterable \| undefined | no | | | | expandedKeys | Iterable \| undefined | no | | | | isDisabled | boolean \| undefined | no | | | | onExpandedChange | ((keys: Set) => void) \| undefined | no | | | | type | "multiple" \| "single" \| undefined | no | single | When `single`, only one panel may be open at a time. | | variant | "bordered" \| "flush" \| undefined | no | | | ## Accessibility Each trigger is a button with `aria-expanded`. components.markdown:
# Layout

Multi-pane page shell for tool UIs: optional header/footer bands and a horizontal
middle row for start, content, and end zones. Pair with `LayoutContent` and
`LayoutPanel` for master-detail inspectors.

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { useState } from 'react';
import {
  Button,
  Layout,
  LayoutContent,
  LayoutPanel,
  ResizeHandle,
  useResizable,
} from '@var-ui/react';

const { end } = useResizable({
  regions: { end: { defaultWidth: 280, minWidth: 220, maxWidth: 400 } },
});

<Layout
  height="auto"
  padding={0}
  content={<LayoutContent padding={0}>{/* list */}</LayoutContent>}
  end={
    <>
      <LayoutPanel resizable={end} hasDivider label="Details" role="complementary">
        Inspector
      </LayoutPanel>
      <ResizeHandle {...end.handleProps} />
    </>
  }
/>
```

```astro
---
import { Layout, LayoutContent, LayoutPanel } from '@var-ui/astro';
---

<Layout height="auto" padding={0}>
  <LayoutPanel slot="start" side="start" width={180} hasDivider>Nav</LayoutPanel>
  <LayoutContent>Main</LayoutContent>
  <LayoutPanel slot="end" side="end" width={240} hasDivider>Inspector</LayoutPanel>
</Layout>
```

```html
<!-- Static shell — resize requires React -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Main zone shorthand — used when `content` is omitted. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| content | ReactNode | no |  | Main zone; wins over `children` when both are set. |
| contentWidth | number \| undefined | no |  | Constrains header/content/footer inner wrappers via `margin-inline: auto`. |
| defaultHasDividers | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Divider default inherited by `LayoutHeader`/`LayoutFooter` when they don't set `hasDivider`. |
| end | ReactNode | no |  | Right/end rail, usually a `LayoutPanel`. |
| footer | ReactNode | no |  | Bottom chrome band, usually a `LayoutFooter`. |
| header | ReactNode | no |  | Top chrome band, usually a `LayoutHeader`. |
| height | "auto" \| "fill" \| undefined | no | 'fill' |  |
| padding | LayoutPadding \| undefined | no |  | Outer/inner spacing step for all zones — sets shell CSS vars on the root. Omit for recipe default (`space[4]`). |
| start | ReactNode | no |  | Left/start rail, usually a `LayoutPanel`. |

## Accessibility

Use `role` and `label` on `LayoutContent` and `LayoutPanel` when multiple landmarks of the same type appear on a page.

```tsx
  regions: { end: { defaultWidth: 280, minWidth: 220, maxWidth: 400 } },
});

<Layout
  height="auto"
  padding={0}
  content={<LayoutContent padding={0}>{/* list */}</LayoutContent>}
  end={
    <>
```

props.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

props.name: aria-modal
props.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

props.name: aria-multiline
props.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

props.name: aria-multiselectable
props.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

props.name: aria-orientation
props.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

props.name: aria-owns
props.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

props.name: aria-placeholder
props.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

props.name: aria-posinset
props.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: aria-readonly
props.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-relevant
props.type: "additions" | "additions removals" | "additions text" | "all" | "removals" | "removals additions" | "removals text" | "text" | "text additions" | "text removals" | undefined
props.description: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

props.name: aria-required
props.description: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

props.name: aria-roledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

props.name: aria-rowcount
props.description: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindex
props.description: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

props.name: aria-rowspan
props.description: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-selected
props.description: Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.

props.name: aria-setsize
props.description: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-sort
props.description: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.

props.name: aria-valuemax

props.name: aria-valuemin

props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-level
props.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

props.name: aria-modal
props.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

props.name: aria-multiline
props.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

props.name: aria-multiselectable
props.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

props.name: aria-orientation
props.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

props.name: aria-owns
props.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

props.name: aria-placeholder
props.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

props.name: aria-posinset
props.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: aria-readonly
props.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-relevant
props.type: "additions" | "additions removals" | "additions text" | "all" | "removals" | "removals additions" | "removals text" | "text" | "text additions" | "text removals" | undefined
props.description: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

props.name: aria-required
props.description: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

props.name: aria-roledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

props.name: aria-rowcount
props.description: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindex
props.description: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

props.name: aria-rowspan
props.description: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-selected
props.description: Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.

props.name: aria-setsize
props.description: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-sort
props.description: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.

props.name: aria-valuemax
props.description: Defines the maximum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuemin
props.description: Defines the minimum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuenow
props.description: Defines the current value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: Defines the human readable text alternative of aria-valuenow for a range widget.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

props.name: is

components.markdown:
# Hidden Hides children with `display: none` inside breakpoint media queries. Markup stays in the HTML (no `useMediaQuery` / conditional render), so SSR and hydration match. `hide` is mobile-first and-up. Keys are `base` (0px) plus TypeStyles `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl`. Default at `base` is visible. When shown, the wrapper uses `display: contents`. ## Examples ### Hide from md Visible below `md`, hidden from `md` up. ```tsx import { Hidden, Text } from '@var-ui/react'; Visible below md ``` ```astro --- import { Hidden, Text } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- Visible below md ``` ```html

Visible below md

``` ### Show from md Hidden below `md`, visible from `md` up (`base: true`, then `md: false`). ```tsx import { Hidden, Text } from '@var-ui/react'; Visible from md ``` ```astro --- import { Hidden, Text } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- Visible from md ``` ```html

Visible from md

props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

props.name: aria-current
props.description: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

props.name: aria-description
props.description: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

props.name: aria-details
props.description: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

props.name: aria-disabled
props.description: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-dropeffect
props.description: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

props.name: aria-errormessage
props.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

props.name: aria-flowto
props.description:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

props.name: aria-grabbed
props.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.

props.name: aria-haspopup
props.description: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

props.name: aria-keyshortcuts
props.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-level
props.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

props.name: aria-modal
props.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

props.name: aria-multiline
props.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

props.name: aria-multiselectable
props.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

props.name: aria-orientation
props.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

props.name: aria-owns
props.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

props.name: aria-placeholder
props.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

props.name: aria-posinset
props.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: aria-readonly
props.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-roledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

props.name: aria-rowindex

props.name: aria-rowindextext

props.name: aria-rowspan

props.name: aria-selected

props.name: aria-setsize

props.name: aria-sort

props.name: aria-dropeffect
props.description: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

props.name: aria-errormessage
props.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

props.name: aria-flowto
props.description:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

props.name: aria-grabbed
props.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.

props.name: aria-haspopup
props.description: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

props.name: aria-keyshortcuts
props.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-level
props.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

props.name: aria-modal
props.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

props.name: aria-multiline
props.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

props.name: aria-multiselectable
props.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

props.name: aria-orientation
props.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

props.name: aria-owns
props.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

props.name: aria-placeholder
props.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

props.name: aria-posinset
props.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: aria-readonly
props.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-relevant
props.type: "additions" | "additions removals" | "additions text" | "all" | "removals" | "removals additions" | "removals text" | "text" | "text additions" | "text removals" | undefined
props.description: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

props.name: aria-required
props.description: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

props.name: aria-roledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

props.name: aria-rowcount
props.description: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindex
props.description: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

props.name: aria-rowspan
props.description: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-selected
props.description: Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.

props.name: aria-setsize
props.description: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-sort
props.description: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.

props.name: aria-valuemax
props.description: Defines the maximum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuemin
props.description: Defines the minimum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuenow
props.description: Defines the current value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: Defines the human readable text alternative of aria-valuenow for a range widget.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

props.name: is
props.description: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

components.name: Toc
components.description: Table of contents with Toc.Item links for in-page navigation.
components.markdown:
# Toc

In-page table of contents. Compose manual `Toc.Item`s or enable `auto` to scan headings in a content root.

## Examples

### Default

A flat list of section anchors with one selected item.

```tsx
import { Toc } from '@var-ui/react';

<Toc title="On this page">
  <Toc.Item label="Examples" href="#examples" isSelected />
  <Toc.Item label="Props" href="#props" />
</Toc>
```

```astro
---
import { Toc, TocItem } from '@var-ui/astro';
---
<Toc title="On this page">
  <TocItem label="Examples" href="#examples" isSelected />
  <TocItem label="Props" href="#props" />
</Toc>
```

```html
<nav class="var-ui-toc" aria-label="On this page">…</nav>
```

### Nested items

Mark subsection links with `isNested` (matches auto mode’s `h3` indent).

```tsx
import { Toc } from '@var-ui/react';

<Toc title="On this page">
  <Toc.Item label="Examples" href="#examples" isSelected />
  <Toc.Item label="Default" href="#default" isNested />
  <Toc.Item label="Nested items" href="#nested" isNested />
  <Toc.Item label="Props" href="#props" />
  <Toc.Item label="Accessibility" href="#accessibility" />
</Toc>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| auto | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Scan a content root for `h2`/`h3` headings with ids. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Manual `Toc.Item` children. Omit when using `auto`. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| contentSelector | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| headerOffset | number \| undefined | no |  |  |
| headingSelector | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| hideBelowXl | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Hide the nav below the `xl` breakpoint. |
| label | string \| undefined | no | title or 'On this page' | Accessible name for the nav landmark. |
| minHeadings | number \| undefined | no |  |  |
| stickyTop | string \| undefined | no |  | Sets `--var-ui-toc-sticky-top` on the root. |
| title | ReactNode | no | 'On this page' | Visible section label above the list. |

## Accessibility

The root is a `nav` landmark. Selected items set `aria-current="location"`. Prefer stable heading `id`s so `href="#…"` targets resolve.
