components.name: Breadcrumbs
components.description: Hierarchical navigation trail for the current page.
components.markdown:
# Breadcrumbs

Hierarchical trail for the current page. Pass `items` with stable `id`s; omit `href` on the current crumb.

## Examples

### Default

A short trail ending on the current page.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs } from '@var-ui/react';

<Breadcrumbs
  items={[
    { id: 'home', label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { id: 'docs', label: 'Docs', href: '/docs' },
    { id: 'current', label: 'Breadcrumbs' },
  ]}
/>
```

```astro
---
import { Breadcrumbs } from '@var-ui/astro';
---
<Breadcrumbs
  items={[
    { id: 'home', label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { id: 'docs', label: 'Docs', href: '/docs' },
    { id: 'current', label: 'Breadcrumbs' },
  ]}
/>
```

```html
<nav class="var-ui-breadcrumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">…</nav>
```

### Collapse

Set `maxItems` so long trails collapse to an ellipsis that expands on click (`itemsBeforeCollapse` / `itemsAfterCollapse` default to 1).

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs } from '@var-ui/react';

<Breadcrumbs
  maxItems={3}
  items={[
    { id: 'home', label: 'Home', href: '/' },
    { id: 'products', label: 'Products', href: '/products' },
    { id: 'hardware', label: 'Hardware', href: '/products/hardware' },
    { id: 'laptops', label: 'Laptops', href: '/products/hardware/laptops' },
    { id: 'current', label: 'Pro 16' },
  ]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| items | BreadcrumbItemData[] | yes |  |  |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| itemsAfterCollapse | number \| undefined | no | 1 | Trailing items kept visible after the collapse point. |
| itemsBeforeCollapse | number \| undefined | no | 1 | Leading items kept visible before the collapse point. |
| label | string \| undefined | no | 'Breadcrumb' | Accessible name for the nav landmark. |
| maxItems | number \| undefined | no |  | Collapse to an ellipsis once `items.length` exceeds this. |
| onAction | ((id: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fires with the pressed item's `id` (not called for the current item). |
| separator | string \| undefined | no | '/' | Separator string rendered between items via CSS `content`. |

## Accessibility

The root is a `nav` landmark (`label` defaults to `"Breadcrumb"`). Built on RAC breadcrumbs; the ellipsis control is a button labeled “Show all breadcrumbs”.

# AppShell Application chrome that lays out optional banner, top nav, side nav, main content, and aside in a CSS grid. Includes a skip-to-content link and a mobile breakpoint that hides the persistent side column. Wrap pages in `AppShell` instead of hand-rolling landmarks. Set `height="stretch"` to fill the parent instead of the viewport. ## Examples ### Default Pass `topNav` and `sideNav` slots; children render in the main landmark. ```tsx import { AppShell, SideNav, TopNav } from '@var-ui/react'; …} sideNav={…} > Main content ``` ```astro --- import { AppShell, SideNav, TopNav } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- … … Main content ``` ```html
…
``` ### Alt layout Set `layout="alt"` so the side column spans the full viewport height and the header sits above main only — useful when the side nav is the primary chrome. ```tsx import { AppShell, SideNav, TopNav } from '@var-ui/react'; }>…} sideNav={}>…} > Main content ``` ```astro ``` ```html ``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | aside | ReactNode | no | | Optional right rail (e.g. an `Outline`). Hidden below `mobileBreakpoint`. | | asideCollapsed | boolean \| undefined | no | | Fully hides the aside column. | | banner | ReactNode | no | | Full-width banner above the top nav / content frame. | | children | ReactNode | no | | Rendered inside the `
` landmark. | | className | string \| undefined | no | | | | contentPadding | AppShellContentPadding \| undefined | no | 0 | Main content padding — design-token space step. | | disabled | boolean \| undefined | no | | When `true`, renders only the main landmark — no chrome slots, skip link, or mobile provider wrapper. Useful for auth and onboarding pages. | | headerHidden | boolean \| undefined | no | | Hides the top nav (pairs with `headroom` or manual scroll logic). | | headerOffset | boolean \| undefined | no | | When `true` (default), a hidden header still reserves grid space. When `false`, the top row collapses so main expands into the header band. | | headroom | UseHeadroomOptions \| boolean \| undefined | no | | Scroll-driven header hide — sets `headerHidden` from `useHeadroom`. Observes the shell `
` scroll container. | | height | "auto" \| "fill" \| "stretch" \| undefined | no | 'fill' | | | layout | AppShellLayout \| undefined | no | | `default` — header spans full width above the side column. `alt` — side column spans full viewport height; header sits above main only. | | mobileBreakpoint | AppShellMobileBreakpoint \| undefined | no | 'md' | Viewport width below which `sideNav` hides and `data-mobile` is set on the root. `'none'` never goes mobile. | | mobileNav | ReactNode | no | | A `MobileNav` drawer. Stays mounted at every width — its own `isOpen` (or the shared `MobileNavProvider`) controls visibility. Consumers place a `MobileNav.Toggle` in `topNav`'s `endContent` themselves; `AppShell` doesn't inject one. | | sideNav | ReactNode | no | | Rendered in the persistent side column above `mobileBreakpoint`; hidden below it. | | sideNavCollapsed | boolean \| undefined | no | | Fully hides the side column on desktop (distinct from `SideNav` icon-only collapse). | | topNav | ReactNode | no | | Rendered in the top bar zone, e.g. a `TopNav`. | | variant | "elevated" \| "section" \| "surface" \| "wash" \| undefined | no | 'elevated' | | ## Accessibility `AppShell` renders a skip-to-content link targeting the main landmark (`id` `var-ui-app-shell-main`). Keep meaningful content in `children` so the skip target is useful. The shell wraps slots in `MobileNavProvider` so a `MobileNav` / `MobileNav.Toggle` pair can share open state at the mobile breakpoint without extra wiring.

presented if they are made.

props.description: Indicates the current "checked" state of checkboxes, radio buttons, and other widgets.

props.description: Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.description: Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-colindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-colindex.

props.name: aria-colspan
props.description: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

props.name: aria-current
props.description: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

props.description: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

props.name: aria-details
props.description: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

props.description: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-dropeffect
props.description: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

props.name: aria-errormessage
props.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

props.name: aria-flowto
props.description:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

props.name: aria-grabbed
props.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.

props.name: aria-haspopup
props.description: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

props.name: aria-keyshortcuts
props.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-level
props.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

props.name: aria-modal
props.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

props.name: aria-multiline
props.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

props.name: aria-multiselectable
props.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

props.name: aria-orientation
props.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

props.name: aria-owns
props.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

props.name: aria-placeholder
props.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

props.name: aria-posinset
props.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: aria-readonly
props.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

components.name: SideNav
components.description: Collapsible side navigation with Section, Item, and Heading parts.
components.markdown:
# SideNav

Persistent side navigation with sticky header/footer zones around a scrollable middle. Compose with `SideNav.Heading`, `SideNav.Section`, and `SideNav.Item` (link via `href` or button via `onPress`). Optional `collapsible` icon-only mode and `resizable` width.

## Examples

### Default

Brand in `header`, then a section of items.

```tsx
import { SideNav } from '@var-ui/react';

<SideNav header={<SideNav.Heading heading="Acme" />}>
  <SideNav.Section title="Main">
    <SideNav.Item label="Dashboard" href="/" isSelected />
  </SideNav.Section>
</SideNav>
```

```astro
---
import { SideNav, SideNavHeading, SideNavItem, SideNavSection } from '@var-ui/astro';
---
<SideNav>
  <SideNavHeading slot="header" heading="Acme" />
  <SideNavSection title="Main">
    <SideNavItem label="Dashboard" href="/" isSelected />
  </SideNavSection>
</SideNav>
```

```html
<nav class="var-ui-side-nav" aria-label="Side navigation">…</nav>
```

### Sections

Group related destinations with multiple `SideNav.Section`s — each can take `title`, `subtitle`, and several `SideNav.Item`s.

```tsx
import { SideNav } from '@var-ui/react';

<SideNav header={<SideNav.Heading heading="Acme" subheading="Workspace" />}>
  <SideNav.Section title="Main">
    <SideNav.Item label="Dashboard" href="/" isSelected />
    <SideNav.Item label="Projects" href="/projects" />
  </SideNav.Section>
  <SideNav.Section title="Team" subtitle="Shared">
    <SideNav.Item label="Members" href="/members" />
    <SideNav.Item label="Billing" href="/billing" />
  </SideNav.Section>
</SideNav>
```

components.markdown:
# TopNav

Top application bar with heading, start/center/end zones, and optional menus. Place `TopNav.Item` links in the start zone (or as `children`), and use `TopNav.Menu` / `TopNav.MegaMenu` for richer flyouts.

## Examples

### Default

A simple bar of selected and unselected items.

```tsx
import { TopNav } from '@var-ui/react';

<TopNav>
  <TopNav.Item label="Home" href="/" isSelected />
  <TopNav.Item label="Docs" href="/docs" />
</TopNav>
```

```astro
---
import { TopNav, TopNavItem } from '@var-ui/astro';
---
<TopNav>
  <TopNavItem label="Home" href="/" isSelected />
  <TopNavItem label="Docs" href="/docs" />
</TopNav>
```

```html
<nav class="var-ui-top-nav" aria-label="Top navigation">…</nav>
```

### Items and menu

Mix `TopNav.Item`s with a `TopNav.Menu` hover/focus popover of rich items (title + optional description).

```tsx
import { TopNav } from '@var-ui/react';

<TopNav heading={<TopNav.Heading heading="Acme" />}>
  <TopNav.Item label="Home" href="/" isSelected />
  <TopNav.Item label="Docs" href="/docs" />
  <TopNav.Menu
    label="Products"
    items={[
      { id: 'cloud', title: 'Cloud', description: 'Deploy anywhere', href: '/cloud' },
      { id: 'analytics', title: 'Analytics', description: 'Measure what matters', href: '/analytics' },
    ]}
  />
</TopNav>
```


## Props

| children | ReactNode | no |  | Content that begins the bar (nav items, `TopNav.Menu` / `TopNav.MegaMenu`). Alias for `startContent`. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| endContent | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| heading | ReactNode | no |  | Brand block, usually a `TopNav.Heading`. |
| label | string \| undefined | no | 'Top navigation' | Accessible name for the `nav` landmark. |
| startContent | ReactNode | no |  |  |

## Accessibility

The root is a `nav` landmark (`label` defaults to `"Top navigation"`). Selected items set `aria-current="page"`; icon-only items keep `label` as `aria-label`. `TopNav.Menu` opens on hover or keyboard focus via `HoverCard` — keep item titles clear so the popover list is usable without relying on icons alone.

components.markdown:
# TopNavMegaMenu

Full-width panel below the top bar for richer navigation. Pass `items` and optional `featured` (usually a `TopNav.MegaMenu.FeaturedCard`). Opens on hover/focus after a short delay; dismiss with Escape or an outside click. Also available as `TopNav.MegaMenu`.

## Examples

### Default

A mega menu trigger with a short item list and a featured card.

```tsx
import { TopNav } from '@var-ui/react';

<TopNav>
  <TopNav.MegaMenu
    label="Solutions"
    items={[{ id: 'startups', title: 'For startups', href: '/startups' }]}
    featured={<TopNav.MegaMenu.FeaturedCard title="Enterprise" description="Scale" />}
  />
</TopNav>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Featured card

Use `TopNav.MegaMenu.FeaturedCard` for the right-hand promo slot — title, description, optional `href`, and an `action` control.

```tsx
import { Button, TopNav } from '@var-ui/react';

<TopNav>
  <TopNav.MegaMenu
    label="Solutions"
    isOpen
    items={[
      { id: 'startups', title: 'For startups', href: '/startups' },
      { id: 'enterprise', title: 'For enterprise', href: '/enterprise' },
    ]}
    featured={
      <TopNav.MegaMenu.FeaturedCard
        title="Platform tour"
        description="See how teams build with Acme in under five minutes."
        href="/tour"
        action={<Button size="sm">Watch demo</Button>}
      />
    }
  />
</TopNav>
```



## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| label | string | yes |  |  |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | Extra panel content rendered alongside `items` (e.g. hand-composed `TopNav.MegaMenu.Item`s). |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| closeDelay | number \| undefined | no | 250 | Delay before the panel closes after the pointer/focus leaves, in milliseconds. |
| featured | ReactNode | no |  | Right-panel slot, usually a `TopNav.MegaMenu.FeaturedCard`. |
| isOpen | boolean \| undefined | no |  | Controlled open state — omit to let the menu manage it internally. |
| items | TopNavRichItem[] \| undefined | no |  |  |
| onOpenChange | ((isOpen: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| openDelay | number \| undefined | no | 150 | Delay before the panel opens on hover/focus, in milliseconds. |

## Accessibility

The trigger exposes `aria-expanded` and `aria-haspopup`. Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the trigger. Prefer clear item titles and featured-card copy so the panel works without relying on imagery alone.

# MobileNav Slide-out mobile navigation drawer built on React Aria Modal — focus trap, Escape, and backdrop dismissal included. Control open state with `isOpen` / `onOpenChange`, or share state through `MobileNavProvider` + `MobileNav.Toggle`. ## Examples ### Default Controlled open state from a button. ```tsx import { MobileNav } from '@var-ui/react'; ``` ```astro --- import { MobileNav, MobileNavToggle, SideNavItem } from '@var-ui/astro'; ---
``` ```html
…
``` ### Provider and toggle Wrap the hamburger and drawer in `MobileNavProvider` so `MobileNav.Toggle` and `MobileNav` share open state without prop drilling. `AppShell` already provides this at the mobile breakpoint. ```tsx import { MobileNav, MobileNavProvider, SideNav } from '@var-ui/react'; ``` ```astro ``` ```html ``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | children | ReactNode | no | | Drawer content — typically a `SideNav.Section`/`SideNav.Item` tree. | | className | string \| undefined | no | | | | closeLabel | string \| undefined | no | 'Close navigation' | Label for the close button. | | header | ReactNode | no | | Rendered in the sticky header row, left of the close button. | | isOpen | boolean \| undefined | no | | Controlled open state — falls back to a `MobileNavProvider` ancestor when omitted. | | label | string \| undefined | no | 'Navigation' | Accessible name for the dialog. | | onOpenChange | ((open: boolean) => void) \| undefined | no | | Falls back to a `MobileNavProvider` ancestor when omitted. | | portalContainer | Element \| undefined | no | | Element the modal portals into instead of `document.body`. Needed when a subtree renders under a different theme than the page ambient (the theme's CSS custom properties only cascade to descendants of the themed element). | | side | "auto" \| "end" \| "start" \| undefined | no | 'auto' | Edge the panel slides in from. `'auto'` resolves to `'start'`. | | width | number \| undefined | no | 320 | Panel width in px; the recipe caps it at 85vw. | ## Accessibility The panel is a dialog (`label` defaults to `"Navigation"`) with a labeled close control. `MobileNav.Toggle` sets `aria-expanded` from provider or explicit `isOpen`, and defaults to `aria-label="Open navigation"`. Prefer the provider pattern when the toggle lives in top chrome and the drawer is a sibling (as in `AppShell`).

components.markdown:
# TabList

Nav landmark tabs for switching views or routes — no panels. Compose `TabList.Tab` rows and an optional `TabList.Menu` overflow trigger. Controlled via `value` / `onChange`.

## Examples

### Default

A short strip of selected and unselected tabs.

```tsx
import { TabList } from '@var-ui/react';

<TabList value={tab} onChange={setTab} label="Sections">
  <TabList.Tab value="overview" label="Overview" />
  <TabList.Tab value="activity" label="Activity" />
</TabList>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Overflow menu

Keep primary tabs visible and tuck the rest into `TabList.Menu` — selecting an option updates the same controlled `value`.

```tsx
import { TabList } from '@var-ui/react';

<TabList value={tab} onChange={setTab} label="Sections">
  <TabList.Tab value="overview" label="Overview" />
  <TabList.Tab value="activity" label="Activity" />
  <TabList.Tab value="members" label="Members" />
  <TabList.Menu
    label="More"
    options={[
      { value: 'settings', label: 'Settings' },
      { value: 'billing', label: 'Billing' },
      { value: 'audit', label: 'Audit log' },
    ]}
  />
</TabList>
```



## Props

| children | ReactNode | no |  | `TabList.Tab` / `TabList.Menu` children. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |

| layout | "fill" \| "hug" \| undefined | no | 'hug' | `hug` sizes tabs to content; `fill` stretches tabs/menu evenly across the width. |

props.name: level

props.name: size

props.name: aria-activedescendant
props.description: Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox, group, or application.

props.name: aria-atomic
props.description: Indicates whether assistive technologies will present all, or only parts of, the changed region based on the change notifications defined by the aria-relevant attribute.

props.name: aria-autocomplete
props.description:
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be
presented if they are made.

props.name: aria-braillelabel
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

props.name: aria-brailleroledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized abbreviated description for the role of an element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

props.name: aria-checked
props.description: Indicates the current "checked" state of checkboxes, radio buttons, and other widgets.

props.name: aria-colcount
props.description: Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-colindex
props.description: Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-colindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-colindex.

props.name: aria-colspan
props.description: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-controls
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

props.name: aria-current
props.description: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

props.name: aria-description
props.description: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

props.name: aria-details
props.description: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

props.name: aria-disabled
props.description: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-dropeffect
props.description: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

props.name: aria-errormessage
props.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

props.name: aria-flowto
props.description:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

props.name: aria-grabbed
props.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.

props.name: aria-haspopup
props.description: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

props.name: aria-keyshortcuts
props.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-level
props.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

props.name: aria-modal
props.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

props.name: aria-multiline
props.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

props.name: aria-multiselectable
props.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

props.name: aria-orientation
props.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

props.name: aria-owns
props.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

props.name: aria-placeholder
props.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

props.name: aria-posinset
props.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: aria-readonly
props.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-relevant
props.type: "additions" | "additions removals" | "additions text" | "all" | "removals" | "removals additions" | "removals text" | "text" | "text additions" | "text removals" | undefined
props.description: Indicates what notifications the user agent will trigger when the accessibility tree within a live region is modified.

props.name: aria-required
props.description: Indicates that user input is required on the element before a form may be submitted.

props.name: aria-roledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized description for the role of an element.

props.name: aria-rowcount
props.description: Defines the total number of rows in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindex
props.description: Defines an element's row index or position with respect to the total number of rows within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-rowindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-rowindex.

props.name: aria-rowspan
props.description: Defines the number of rows spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-selected
props.description: Indicates the current "selected" state of various widgets.

props.name: aria-setsize
props.description: Defines the number of items in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-sort
props.description: Indicates if items in a table or grid are sorted in ascending or descending order.

props.name: aria-valuemax
props.description: Defines the maximum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuemin
props.description: Defines the minimum allowed value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuenow
props.description: Defines the current value for a range widget.

props.name: aria-valuetext
props.description: Defines the human readable text alternative of aria-valuenow for a range widget.

props.name: inputMode
props.description: Hints at the type of data that might be entered by the user while editing the element or its contents

props.description: Specify that a standard HTML element should behave like a defined custom built-in element

# Text Body text with size and tone variants. ## Examples ### Default ```tsx import { Text } from '@var-ui/react'; Body text with secondary tone. ``` ```astro --- import { Text } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- Body text with secondary tone. ``` ```html

Body text with secondary tone.

``` ### Tones `primary` is the default text color and `secondary` is for supporting copy. `accent`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` and `info` use the matching semantic tone's foreground color, for example `danger` for errors and validation messages. ```tsx import { Stack, Text } from '@var-ui/react'; Primary text is the default. Secondary text for supporting copy. Accent text for emphasis. Success text for confirmations. Warning text for cautions. Danger text for errors and validation messages. Info text for neutral notices. ``` ```astro --- import { Text } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- Primary text is the default. Secondary text for supporting copy. Accent text for emphasis. Success text for confirmations. Warning text for cautions. Danger text for errors and validation messages. Info text for neutral notices. ``` ```html

Primary text is the default.

Danger text for errors and validation messages.

Info text for neutral notices.

components.name: CodeBlock
components.description: Syntax-highlighted code display.
components.markdown:
# CodeBlock Code display with copy-to-clipboard, line numbers, and optional syntax highlighting. `CodeBlock` handles layout and interaction. **Syntax highlighting is separate** — you run a highlighter (highlight.js, Shiki, Prism, etc.) and pass the result via `codeHtml` and `codeClassName`. The plain `code` string is always used for the copy button. ## Examples ### Default ```tsx import { CodeBlock } from '@var-ui/react'; const code = 'const greeting = "hello";'; ``` ```astro --- import { CodeBlock } from '@var-ui/astro'; const code = 'const greeting = "hello";'; --- ``` ```html
tsx
const greeting = "hello";
``` ## Syntax highlighting ### Styles Syntax highlighting colors come from `color.code` tokens (`--var-ui-color-code-*`). Your app maps those CSS variables to whatever highlighter you use — highlight.js class selectors, a Shiki theme, Prism tokens, etc. See [Design tokens](/theming/tokens#syntax-highlighting). ### Runtime highlighting Pass pre-highlighted HTML alongside the plain source: ```tsx import { CodeBlock } from '@var-ui/react'; import hljs from 'highlight.js/lib/core'; import typescript from 'highlight.js/lib/languages/typescript'; hljs.registerLanguage('typescript', typescript); const code = 'const greeting = "hello";'; ; ``` Use any highlighter that outputs HTML with `hljs-*` classes (or map your classes to the same token groups in a custom theme). ### Build-time highlighting For docs sites and SSR, prefer highlighting at build time — Shiki, `rehype-highlight`, or Astro/MDX pipelines — then pass the resulting HTML to `codeHtml`. No client-side highlighter bundle required. ### Line numbers When `showLineNumbers` is enabled, pass one HTML string per line via `lineHtml` instead of `codeHtml`: ```tsx const lines = code.replace(/\n$/, '').split('\n'); hljs.highlight(line, { language: 'typescript' }).value)} />; ``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | code | string | yes | | Source code string to display and copy. | | className | string \| undefined | no | | Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element. | | codeClassName | string \| undefined | no | | Classes for the highlighted `` element (e.g. `hljs language-tsx`). | | codeHtml | string \| undefined | no | | Pre-highlighted HTML for the code body. Pair with `codeClassName` from your highlighter. | | copiedLabel | string \| undefined | no | Copied | Feedback text after a successful copy. | | copyable | boolean \| undefined | no | true | Whether to show the copy-to-clipboard button. | | copyErrorLabel | string \| undefined | no | Copy failed | Feedback text when clipboard write fails. | | copyLabel | string \| undefined | no | Copy code | Accessible label for the copy button. | | filename | string \| undefined | no | | Optional filename shown in the header. | | highlightedLines | number[] \| undefined | no | | 1-based line numbers to highlight. | | language | string \| undefined | no | | Language tag shown in the header (e.g. `tsx`, `bash`). | | lineHtml | string[] \| undefined | no | | Pre-highlighted HTML per line when `showLineNumbers` is enabled. | | showLineNumbers | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Show line numbers in a gutter column. | | wrapLongLines | boolean \| undefined | no | false | Wrap long lines instead of horizontal scrolling. | | variant | "default" \| "diff" \| "inline" \| "terminal" \| undefined | no | | | ## Accessibility Built on React Aria Components where applicable.

components.description: Formatted date/time display.
components.markdown:
# Timestamp

Formatted date/time display.

## Examples

### Default

```tsx
import { Timestamp } from '@var-ui/react';

<Timestamp date={new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000)} />
```

```astro
---
// No @var-ui/astro Timestamp — format the label yourself and use textBlock styles.
import { textBlock } from '@var-ui/core';

const t = textBlock({ size: 'sm', tone: 'secondary' });
---

<time
  class:list={[t]}
  datetime="2026-07-19T21:35:00.000Z"
  title="Jul 19, 2026, 2:35 PM"
>
  5 minutes ago
</time>
```

```html
<time data-size="sm" data-tone="secondary" data-weight="normal" class="var-ui-text-block" datetime="2026-07-19T21:35:00.000Z" title="Jul 19, 2026, 2:35 PM">5 minutes ago</time>
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| date | Date \| number \| string | yes |  | Date value to format. Accepts a `Date`, ISO string, or epoch milliseconds. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  | Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element. |
| format | "date" \| "datetime" \| "relative" \| "time" \| undefined | no | relative | Output format: relative ("5 minutes ago"), date, time, or datetime. |
| locale | string \| undefined | no |  | BCP 47 locale for formatting. Uses the runtime default when omitted. |

## Accessibility

Built on React Aria Components where applicable. Astro and HTML demos use a static `<time>` with `textBlock` styles (no live relative formatting).

import { Timestamp } from '@var-ui/react';

<Timestamp date={new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60_000)} />

components.markdown:
# List

Structured vertical list with `List.Item` rows for labels, descriptions, and optional start/end content. Supports compound children or an `items` array.

## Examples

### Default

A member list with labels and secondary descriptions.

```tsx
import { List } from '@var-ui/react';

<List header="Members">
  <List.Item label="Ada Lovelace" description="Admin" />
  <List.Item label="Grace Hopper" description="Editor" />
</List>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Icons

Pass decorative `startContent` (for example `Icon`) for shortcut or settings rows. Keep start/end slots non-interactive when the row uses `href` / `onPress`.

```tsx
import { Icon, List } from '@var-ui/react';

<List header="Shortcuts" hasDividers>
  <List.Item
    label="Search"
    description="Find anything"
    startContent={<Icon name="search" size="sm" />}
  />
  <List.Item
    label="Recent"
    description="Opened today"
    startContent={<Icon name="clock" size="sm" />}
  />
</List>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| children | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| density | "balanced" \| "compact" \| "spacious" \| undefined | no |  |  |
| hasDividers | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| header | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| items | ListItemData[] \| undefined | no |  |  |
| listStyle | "decimal" \| "disc" \| "none" \| undefined | no |  |  |
| onAction | ((id: string) => void) \| undefined | no |  | Fired for interactive items without href (items mode / Item onPress). |
| renderEnd | ((item: ListItemData) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| renderStart | ((item: ListItemData) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  |  |

## Accessibility

Renders a `<ul>` (or `<ol>` when `listStyle="decimal"`). Interactive rows use an invisible overlay as the sole hit target — do not nest links or buttons in `startContent` / `endContent` on those rows. Prefer string `label`s so the overlay gets a clear accessible name.

import { List } from '@var-ui/react';

<List header="Members">
  <List.Item label="Ada Lovelace" description="Admin" />
  <List.Item label="Grace Hopper" description="Editor" />
</List>

import { Icon, List } from '@var-ui/react';

<List header="Shortcuts" hasDividers>
  <List.Item
    label="Search"
    description="Find anything"
    startContent={<Icon name="search" size="sm" />}
  />
  <List.Item
    label="Recent"
    description="Opened today"
    startContent={<Icon name="clock" size="sm" />}
  />
</List>

components.description: Page outline links with optional scroll-spy highlighting.
components.markdown:
# Outline

In-page outline navigation. Pass a flat `items` array (or `Outline.Item` children) and highlight via controlled `activeId` or automatic scroll-spy.

## Examples

### Default

Flat section links with a controlled active item (scroll-spy off).

```tsx
import { Outline } from '@var-ui/react';

<Outline
  activeId="intro"
  scrollSpy={false}
  items={[
    { id: 'intro', text: 'Intro', level: 2 },
    { id: 'examples', text: 'Examples', level: 2 },
  ]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Nested items

Use `level: 3` for subsections — nested links indent under their parent heading.

```tsx
import { Outline } from '@var-ui/react';

<Outline
  activeId="examples"
  scrollSpy={false}
  items={[
    { id: 'intro', text: 'Intro', level: 2 },
    { id: 'examples', text: 'Examples', level: 2 },
    { id: 'default', text: 'Default', level: 3 },
    { id: 'nested', text: 'Nested', level: 3 },
  ]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| activeId | string \| undefined | no |  | Controlled active item id — disables scroll-spy when set. |
| children | ReactNode | no |  | `Outline.Item` children, used when `items` is omitted. |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| items | OutlineItemData[] \| undefined | no |  | Flat list of headings to render as links — takes priority over `Outline.Item` children. |
| scrollSpy | boolean \| undefined | no | true | Observe heading elements and highlight the topmost visible one when `activeId` is omitted. |
| title | string \| undefined | no | 'On this page' | Accessible name for the `nav` landmark and the visible heading. |

## Accessibility

The root is a `nav` landmark named by `title` (default “On this page”). Links target `#id` — keep matching heading `id`s in the page. When scroll-spy is on, the active link updates from an `IntersectionObserver`; pass `activeId` to control highlighting yourself.

components.markdown:
# Table

Presentational semantic `<table>` for admin data grids. Use compound `Table.Header` / `Body` / `Row` / `Column` / `Cell` parts or a data-driven `columns` + `data` API.

## Examples

### Default

A simple two-column data table.

```tsx
import { Table } from '@var-ui/react';

<Table
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', header: 'Name', isRowHeader: true },
    { key: 'role', header: 'Role' },
  ]}
  data={[{ name: 'Ada', role: 'Admin' }]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Striped compact

Enable `isStriped` and `density="compact"` for denser rosters; add `caption` for an accessible table title.

```tsx
import { Table } from '@var-ui/react';

<Table
  isStriped
  density="compact"
  caption="Team roster"
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', header: 'Name', isRowHeader: true },
    { key: 'role', header: 'Role' },
    { key: 'status', header: 'Status' },
  ]}
  data={[
    { name: 'Ada', role: 'Admin', status: 'Active' },
    { name: 'Grace', role: 'Editor', status: 'Active' },
  ]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| caption | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| children | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| columnOrder | string[] \| undefined | no |  | Column keys in display order — required with `columnWidths` for `<colgroup>`. |
| columns | TableColumnDef<T>[] \| undefined | no |  |  |
| columnWidths | Record<string, string> \| undefined | no |  | Explicit column widths keyed by column id. |
| data | T[] \| undefined | no |  |  |
| density | "balanced" \| "compact" \| "spacious" \| undefined | no |  |  |
| dividers | "columns" \| "grid" \| "none" \| "rows" \| undefined | no |  |  |
| emptyContent | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| getRowId | ((row: T) => string) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| hasHover | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| isStriped | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| layout | "auto" \| "fixed" \| undefined | no | 'auto' |  |
| onSortChange | ((next: SortDescriptor) => void) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| renderCell | ((column: TableColumnDef<T>, row: T) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| sortDescriptor | SortDescriptor \| undefined | no |  |  |
| stickyHeader | boolean \| undefined | no |  |  |
| textOverflow | "truncate" \| "wrap" \| undefined | no |  |  |

## Accessibility

Renders a real `<table>`. Mark the identifying column with `isRowHeader` (`scope="row"`). Prefer a `caption` (or external heading referenced with `aria-labelledby`) so the table has an accessible name. Sort chrome sets `aria-sort` when you wire `allowsSorting` / `onSortChange`.

components.markdown:
# Tree

Hierarchical expandable list with APG tree keyboard behavior. Compose nested `Tree.Item`s or pass a recursive `items` array; control expand/selection with `expandedKeys` / `selectedKeys`.

## Examples

### Default

A small file tree with one folder expanded.

```tsx
import { Tree } from '@var-ui/react';

<Tree
  aria-label="Files"
  defaultExpandedKeys={['src']}
  items={[{ id: 'src', label: 'src', children: [{ id: 'app', label: 'App.tsx' }] }]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

### Expanded selection

Seed nested expansion with `defaultExpandedKeys` and highlight a leaf via `selectionMode` + `defaultSelectedKeys`.

```tsx
import { Tree } from '@var-ui/react';

<Tree
  aria-label="Project files"
  selectionMode="single"
  defaultExpandedKeys={['src', 'components']}
  defaultSelectedKeys={['button']}
  items={[
    {
      id: 'src',
      label: 'src',
      children: [
        {
          id: 'components',
          label: 'components',
          children: [{ id: 'button', label: 'Button.tsx' }],
        },
      ],
    },
  ]}
/>
```

```astro
<!-- No Astro binding yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

```html
<!-- No HTML demo yet — use @var-ui/react -->
```

## Props

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aria-label | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| children | ReactNode | no |  |  |
| className | string \| undefined | no |  |  |
| defaultExpandedKeys | Iterable<string> \| undefined | no |  |  |
| defaultSelectedKeys | Iterable<string> \| undefined | no |  |  |
| density | "balanced" \| "compact" \| "spacious" \| undefined | no |  |  |
| expandedKeys | Iterable<string> \| undefined | no |  |  |
| items | TreeItemData[] \| undefined | no |  |  |
| onExpandedChange | ((keys: Set<string>) => void) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| onSelectionChange | ((keys: Set<string>) => void) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| renderEnd | ((item: TreeItemData) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| renderStart | ((item: TreeItemData) => ReactNode) \| undefined | no |  |  |
| selectedKeys | Iterable<string> \| undefined | no |  |  |
| selectionMode | TreeSelectionMode \| undefined | no |  |  |

## Accessibility

Root uses `role="tree"`; nodes are `treeitem` with `aria-level`, `aria-expanded`, and optional `aria-selected`. Provide an `aria-label` (or labelled-by) on the tree. Arrow keys move focus (roving tabindex); Left/Right collapse/expand; Space/Enter select when `selectionMode` is not `"none"`.

props.name: title
props.description: Card headline.

props.name: description
props.description: Supporting copy below the title.

props.name: hint
props.description: Trailing hint line (e.g. reading time, "Learn more →").

props.name: aria-activedescendant
props.description: Identifies the currently active element when DOM focus is on a composite widget, textbox, group, or application.

props.name: aria-atomic
props.description: Indicates whether assistive technologies will present all, or only parts of, the changed region based on the change notifications defined by the aria-relevant attribute.

props.name: aria-autocomplete
props.description:
Indicates whether inputting text could trigger display of one or more predictions of the user's intended value for an input and specifies how predictions would be
presented if they are made.

props.name: aria-braillelabel
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

props.name: aria-brailleroledescription
props.description: Defines a human-readable, author-localized abbreviated description for the role of an element, which is intended to be converted into Braille.

props.name: aria-checked
props.description: Indicates the current "checked" state of checkboxes, radio buttons, and other widgets.

props.name: aria-colcount
props.description: Defines the total number of columns in a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-colindex
props.description: Defines an element's column index or position with respect to the total number of columns within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-colindextext
props.description: Defines a human readable text alternative of aria-colindex.

props.name: aria-colspan
props.description: Defines the number of columns spanned by a cell or gridcell within a table, grid, or treegrid.

props.name: aria-controls
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) whose contents or presence are controlled by the current element.

props.name: aria-current
props.description: Indicates the element that represents the current item within a container or set of related elements.

props.name: aria-describedby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that describes the object.

props.name: aria-description
props.description: Defines a string value that describes or annotates the current element.

props.name: aria-details
props.description: Identifies the element that provides a detailed, extended description for the object.

props.name: aria-disabled
props.description: Indicates that the element is perceivable but disabled, so it is not editable or otherwise operable.

props.name: aria-dropeffect
props.description: Indicates what functions can be performed when a dragged object is released on the drop target.

props.name: aria-errormessage
props.description: Identifies the element that provides an error message for the object.

props.name: aria-expanded
props.description: Indicates whether the element, or another grouping element it controls, is currently expanded or collapsed.

props.name: aria-flowto
props.description:
Identifies the next element (or elements) in an alternate reading order of content which, at the user's discretion,
allows assistive technology to override the general default of reading in document source order.

props.name: aria-grabbed
props.description: Indicates an element's "grabbed" state in a drag-and-drop operation.

props.name: aria-haspopup
props.description: Indicates the availability and type of interactive popup element, such as menu or dialog, that can be triggered by an element.

props.name: aria-hidden
props.description: Indicates whether the element is exposed to an accessibility API.

props.name: aria-invalid
props.description: Indicates the entered value does not conform to the format expected by the application.

props.name: aria-keyshortcuts
props.description: Indicates keyboard shortcuts that an author has implemented to activate or give focus to an element.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Defines a string value that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: Identifies the element (or elements) that labels the current element.

props.name: aria-level
props.description: Defines the hierarchical level of an element within a structure.

props.name: aria-live
props.description: Indicates that an element will be updated, and describes the types of updates the user agents, assistive technologies, and user can expect from the live region.

props.name: aria-modal
props.description: Indicates whether an element is modal when displayed.

props.name: aria-multiline
props.description: Indicates whether a text box accepts multiple lines of input or only a single line.

props.name: aria-multiselectable
props.description: Indicates that the user may select more than one item from the current selectable descendants.

props.name: aria-orientation
props.description: Indicates whether the element's orientation is horizontal, vertical, or unknown/ambiguous.

props.name: aria-owns
props.description:
Identifies an element (or elements) in order to define a visual, functional, or contextual parent/child relationship
between DOM elements where the DOM hierarchy cannot be used to represent the relationship.

props.name: aria-placeholder
props.description:
Defines a short hint (a word or short phrase) intended to aid the user with data entry when the control has no value.
A hint could be a sample value or a brief description of the expected format.

props.name: aria-posinset
props.description: Defines an element's number or position in the current set of listitems or treeitems. Not required if all elements in the set are present in the DOM.

props.name: aria-pressed
props.description: Indicates the current "pressed" state of toggle buttons.

props.name: aria-readonly
props.description: Indicates that the element is not editable, but is otherwise operable.

``` ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | date | Date \| number \| string | yes | | Passed straight to `Timestamp`. | | className | string \| undefined | no | | Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element. | | format | "date" \| "datetime" \| "relative" \| "time" \| undefined | no | relative | Passed straight to `Timestamp`. | | status | ReactNode | no | | Optional status content shown alongside the timestamp (e.g. "Read"). | ## Accessibility The timestamp and status are rendered as plain text content, so they're exposed to assistive technology in the same way as any other inline text within the message row.

# ChatMessageBubble The chat bubble — a styled content container that reads `sender` from an ancestor `ChatMessage` to auto-style its background and text color. var-ui does zero markdown parsing; pass plain text or your own rendered tree as `children`. ## Examples ### Default There is no `@var-ui/astro` ChatMessageBubble — Astro and HTML previews use the core bubble recipe (pass `sender` explicitly). ```tsx import { ChatMessage, ChatMessageBubble } from '@var-ui/react'; First part of a multi-part reply. Second part. ``` ```astro --- // No @var-ui/astro ChatMessageBubble — core recipe with group corners. import { chatMessage, chatMessageBubble } from '@var-ui/core'; const m = chatMessage({ sender: 'assistant' }); const first = chatMessageBubble({ sender: 'assistant', variant: 'filled', group: 'first' }); const last = chatMessageBubble({ sender: 'assistant', variant: 'filled', group: 'last' }); ---
Navi
First part of a multi-part reply.
Second part.
``` ```html
Navi
First part of a multi-part reply.
Second part.
``` Use `group` when rendering several consecutive bubbles from the same sender, to tighten the corners between them. ## Props | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | children | ReactNode | no | | Bubble content — plain text or a consumer-rendered markdown tree. | | className | string \| undefined | no | | Additional CSS class names merged onto the root element. | | group | "first" \| "last" \| "middle" \| "none" \| undefined | no | | Position within a multi-bubble group from the same sender — tightens corners. | | variant | "filled" \| "ghost" \| undefined | no | filled | Visual variant. `ghost` drops the background but keeps padding for alignment. | ## Accessibility Content is rendered as-is — wire your own markdown renderer with accessible semantics if needed.

guides.title: Getting started
guides.description: Create a project and render your first var-ui component.
guides.markdown:
# Getting started This guide is the happy path for a **Vite + React 19** app: install from npm, import CSS, wrap providers, and render a Button. ## Install ```bash pnpm add @var-ui/react @var-ui/core @var-ui/icons react react-dom react-aria-components ``` ```bash npm install @var-ui/react @var-ui/core @var-ui/icons react react-dom react-aria-components ``` `@var-ui/icons` is optional. Without it, pass `icons={{}}` to `IconProvider`. You do not add `typestyles` to the app. It arrives with `@var-ui/core`. ## Import CSS ```ts import '@var-ui/core/styles.css'; ``` That file includes every recipe, base HTML styles, and the default theme. Custom `createDesignTheme` modules and unused-recipe shedding use extract instead — see [Installation](/docs/installation). ## Providers Mount `DesignSystemProvider` with `applyToDocument`, `IconProvider`, and `LayerProvider` at the root: ```tsx import { defaultIcons } from '@var-ui/icons'; import { DesignSystemProvider, IconProvider, LayerProvider } from '@var-ui/react'; {children} ; ``` Without `@var-ui/icons`, pass `icons={{}}` to `IconProvider`. `applyToDocument` puts the theme class on `html`. Isolate stacking and cover the visual viewport: ```css html { isolation: isolate; } body { position: relative; } ``` ## First component ```tsx import { Button } from '@var-ui/react'; ; ``` ## Astro without React ```bash pnpm add @var-ui/astro @var-ui/core ``` Import the same stylesheet in a layout, then import Astro components: ```astro --- import '@var-ui/core/styles.css'; import { Button } from '@var-ui/astro'; --- ``` See `examples/astro-app` in the repo for a full **workspace** tree. That example still extracts CSS with the TypeStyles Vite plugin because it lives in this monorepo. ## Next - [Installation](/docs/installation) — package list, peers, and TypeStyles extract for custom themes - [Overlay lifecycle](/docs/overlay-lifecycle) — overlay `data-*` attributes, positioner CSS variables, and `onOpenChange` - [Theming](/theming) — tokens, themes, and `createDesignTheme` ## Direction, portals, and stacking ### Direction and locale Pass `direction` and a real `locale` on `DesignSystemProvider`: ```tsx {children} ``` `applyToDocument` syncs `html dir` (and `lang` when `locale` is set) after hydration / on mount. It always writes `dir` for the resolved direction — including default `ltr`. If SSR set `` and the client provider omits `direction`/`locale`, mount will rewrite `dir` to `ltr`. SSR apps that care about first paint should set `` (and `lang` if needed) themselves **and** pass matching `direction`/`locale` to the provider. React Aria overlays (`Popover`, `Menu`, `start` / `end` placement) take direction from **locale**, not from `dir`. `I18nProvider` only accepts `locale`. - Prefer a real RTL locale (`he-IL`, `ar-EG`) so dates, numbers, and overlays agree. - `direction="rtl"` with no locale wraps `I18nProvider` with `ar` so placement still flips. That workaround does **not** set `html lang="ar"`. - `direction="ltr"` (explicit) with no locale wraps `I18nProvider` with `en-US` so a nested LTR island does not inherit a parent RTL locale for overlay placement. - `locale="en-US"` plus `direction="rtl"` keeps English formatting; overlays may **not** flip. - If you omit `direction` but pass `locale`, `dir` is derived from RAC `isRTL(locale)`. - `useDirection()` returns `{ direction, isRtl }` and defaults to `ltr` when no provider is mounted. - Directional icons opt in: ``. Do not set `dir` on the whole docs site to try this — use a `DirectionProvider` island (see Hidden). ### Portals and stacking Wrap the application in an isolating root so portaled dialogs and popovers stack above page `z-index`: ```html
{children}
``` ```css .root { isolation: isolate; } ``` When `DesignSystemProvider` uses `applyToDocument`, put `isolation: isolate` on `html` or `body` instead of an extra wrapper. #### Themed portals Token CSS variables cascade from the theme class. If an overlay portals to `document.body` and the theme class is on a subtree, pass `portalContainer` pointing at the themed node (or use `applyToDocument`). #### iOS 26+ Safari backdrops Dialog and drawer backdrops use `position: absolute` under `@supports (-webkit-touch-callout: none)`. Add `body { position: relative; }` so a scrolled page still covers the visual viewport. Overlay `data-*` attributes, positioner CSS variables, and `onOpenChange` details are documented in [Overlay lifecycle](/docs/overlay-lifecycle).

guides.title: Installation
guides.description: Package setup for React apps using var-ui.
guides.markdown:
# Installation

Install published `@var-ui/*` packages from npm. For the copy-paste Vite + React path, start with [Getting started](/docs/getting-started).

## Packages

| Package         | Role                                                                                                  |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@var-ui/core`  | Tokens, recipes, published CSS (`@var-ui/core/styles.css`), and extract entry (`@var-ui/core/styles`) |
| `@var-ui/react` | React components                                                                                      |
| `@var-ui/icons` | Optional default glyphs for `IconProvider`                                                            |
| `@var-ui/astro` | Astro components (no React)                                                                           |
| `@var-ui/cli`   | Dev dependency: `npx @var-ui/cli` for component lookup, search, and `init`                            |

`@var-ui/icons` is optional for React. Without it, pass `icons={{}}` to `IconProvider`. Astro components load the same default glyphs from `@var-ui/icons/glyphs`, so install `@var-ui/icons` alongside `@var-ui/astro`.

## Peer dependencies

| Peer                      | Notes                               |
| ------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `react` / `react-dom`     | 19                                  |
| `react-aria-components`   | Required by `@var-ui/react`         |
| `@internationalized/date` | Required when using date components |

`typestyles` is a transitive dependency of `@var-ui/core`. Do not add it unless you extract CSS (below) or import TypeStyles directly.

## Advanced: extract CSS

Use this path for custom `createDesignTheme` modules, app-owned recipes, or tree-shaken CSS. Do **not** import `@var-ui/core/styles.css` in the same app — that doubles the stylesheet.

```bash
pnpm add typestyles
pnpm add -D @typestyles/vite
```

```ts
// typestyles-entry.ts
import '@var-ui/core/styles';
```

```ts
import typestyles from '@typestyles/vite';

export default {
  plugins: [typestyles({ extract: { modules: ['typestyles-entry.ts'] } })],
};
```

## This monorepo

This repository still links packages with `workspace:*`. Downstream apps install the published versions from npm and do not use the workspace protocol.

guides.title: Colors
guides.description: Primitive palette ramps and semantic color tokens in var-ui.
guides.markdown:
# Colors

var-ui separates **primitive palette** steps from **semantic color** tokens. Components and
recipes reference semantic tokens (e.g. `color.tone.accent.foreground`) so themes can remap roles without
touching component code.

_Interactive widget — see the HTML docs page._

## Using colors

Import token refs from core:

```ts
import { designTokens } from '@var-ui/core';

designTokens.color.palette['sky-7'].var; // var(--var-ui-color-palette-sky-7)
designTokens.color.tone.accent.foreground.var; // var(--var-ui-color-tone-accent-foreground)
```

Override semantic colors in a theme via `createDesignTheme({ tokens, colorMode })`. See
[Customize](/theming/customize) for details.

guides.title: CSS variables
guides.description: Theme and style var-ui with CSS custom properties — design tokens and component variables.
guides.markdown:
# CSS variables

var-ui themes are CSS custom properties. **Design tokens** (`--var-ui-space-4`,
`--var-ui-color-accent-default`) are the global vocabulary recipes and layouts share.
**Component variables** (`--var-ui-button-background`) are scoped to a single recipe
and inherit through nested theme boundaries.

Use CSS variables when you want plain stylesheets, one-off overrides, or app chrome that
is not tied to a `createDesignTheme` config.

## Quick start

Import core styles so tokens are registered on `:root` (or wrap your app with
`DesignSystemProvider`):

```ts
import '@var-ui/core/styles';
```

Reference tokens in your CSS:

```css
.marketing-hero {
  padding: var(--var-ui-space-8);
  background: var(--var-ui-color-background-subtle);
  color: var(--var-ui-color-text-primary);
  border-radius: var(--var-ui-radius-lg);
  box-shadow: var(--var-ui-shadow-md);
}

.marketing-hero a {
  color: var(--var-ui-color-link-default);
}
```

Override a single button surface inside a custom theme class:

```css
.theme-var-ui-acme .var-ui-button {
  --var-ui-button-background: var(--var-ui-color-accent-default);
  --var-ui-button-foreground: var(--var-ui-color-text-on-accent);
}
```

Typed refs mirror the same names in TypeScript:

```ts
import { designTokens } from '@var-ui/core';

designTokens.space[8].var; // var(--var-ui-space-8)
designTokens.color.tone.accent.foreground.var; // var(--var-ui-color-tone-accent-foreground)
```

## Light and dark mode

Semantic color tokens compile to `light-dark()` on the theme surface, so a single custom
property responds to the active color mode. Set `color-scheme` and `data-color-mode` on a
theme wrapper (as `DesignSystemProvider` does) or follow the same pattern in plain HTML.

Override light and dark faces with `createDesignTheme({ tokens, colorMode })` — see
[Customize](/theming/customize). For raw CSS, set the variable on the themed ancestor;
the compiled value already encodes both faces.

## Custom theme tokens

`createDesignTheme({ tokens: { brand: … } })` mints additional namespaces
(`--var-ui-brand-glow`, etc.) that behave like built-in tokens. They appear on the theme
class alongside built-ins.

## Variable naming

| Layer         | Pattern                                  | Example                                               |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| Design token  | `--var-ui-{namespace}-{key}`             | `--var-ui-fontSize-md`, `--var-ui-color-text-primary` |
| Palette step  | `--var-ui-color-palette-{family}-{step}` | `--var-ui-color-palette-sky-7`                        |
| Component var | `--var-ui-{recipe}-{surface}`            | `--var-ui-button-background`                          |

Token namespaces match `packages/core/src/tokens/schema`. Component names match recipe
namespaces (`button`, `text-field`, `docs-prose`).

## Reference

The tables below are generated from `@var-ui/core` at build time — design tokens from
`tokenValues` / `designTokens`, component variables from registered recipe CSS.

_Interactive widget — see the HTML docs page._

- [Design tokens](/theming/tokens) — token roles and syntax highlighting

guides.title: Theming
guides.description: Customize var-ui with typed themes, tokens, and component overrides.
guides.markdown:
# Theming

var-ui themes are TypeStyles surfaces: semantic CSS custom properties, readable
public class names (plus `data-*` variant attrs), and cascade layers. Switch
light and dark from the header to see tokens respond.

## How to customize (pick the right layer)

1. **`createDesignTheme` with `components`** — primary path for recipe restyles.
   Mint custom mode-aware tokens and restyle any recipe with full CSS and typed
   variant names. No class names in your theme code.
2. **Component CSS variables** — cheapest single-property tweak when a recipe
   already exposes a `c.vars()` hook (e.g. `--var-ui-button-background`).
3. **Public classes / `styles.scope()`** — escape hatch for nested conflicting
   themes (`@scope`) or one-off CSS outside the theme config.

See **[Customize](/theming/customize)** for the full story, **[Themes](/theming/themes)**
for authoring and applying a theme, and **[Design tokens](/theming/tokens)** for
the built-in token map.

## Topics

- [Customize](/theming/customize) — config DX, `tokens`, `components`, `styles.override`
- [Themes](/theming/themes) — `createDesignTheme`, `DesignSystemProvider`
- [Design tokens](/theming/tokens) — semantic colors, space, type
- [CSS variables](/theming/css-variables) — custom property reference and usage

guides.title: Shadows
guides.description: Box-shadow and elevation tokens in var-ui.
guides.markdown:
# Shadows

var-ui ships layered **box-shadow** tokens and a softer **elevation** scale. Each token stacks
multiple shadows with a consistent top-left light source (vertical offset is 2× horizontal).
Shadows tint from primary text color via `color-mix`, so they stay legible in both light and
dark mode without separate dark overrides.

_Interactive widget — see the HTML docs page._

## Using shadows

Import token refs from core:

```ts
import { designTokens } from '@var-ui/core';

designTokens.shadow.md.var; // var(--var-ui-shadow-md)
designTokens.shadow.elevation.low.var; // var(--var-ui-shadow-elevation-low)
```

Use them directly as `box-shadow` values in recipes or plain CSS:

```css
.card {
  box-shadow: var(--var-ui-shadow-md);
}

.floating-panel {
  box-shadow: var(--var-ui-shadow-elevation-high);
}
```

Override shadows in a theme via `createDesignTheme({ tokens: { shadow: … } })`. Neo-brutalist
presets (Rose, Amber) swap in hard offset shadows while keeping the same token names — see
[Themes](/theming/themes) for examples.

guides.title: Design tokens
guides.description: Semantic tokens that power var-ui components and layouts.
guides.markdown:
# Design tokens

var-ui exposes semantic tokens for color, spacing, typography, motion, and
elevation. Components reference tokens (e.g. `t.color.tone.accent.foreground`) instead
of hard-coded values so themes can swap palettes without touching recipes.

Import the shared refs from core:

```ts
import { designTokens } from '@var-ui/core';

designTokens.color.text.primary; // var(--var-ui-color-text-primary)
designTokens.space[4];
designTokens.fontSize.md;
```

Default registered values live in `tokenValues` (used as the built-in `from` preset base).

Theme overrides use two layers:

- **`tokens`** on `createDesignTheme` — mode-invariant patches; the light `color`
  face lives here by default
- **`colorMode`** — TypeStyles `ThemeColorModePatches` (`{ light?, dark? }` namespace
  overrides; patch the `color` namespace for semantic tokens, compiled to `light-dark()`)

Custom namespaces from `createDesignTheme({ tokens })` appear on the theme's
`.tokens` object alongside built-in refs.

Syntax-highlighting colors live under `color.code` (`designTokens.color.code`).
`lightSyntaxValues` / `darkSyntaxValues` are exported aliases for theme presets.

### Syntax highlighting

var-ui defines semantic **code colors** but does not ship highlighter-specific CSS.
Map `color.code` to your toolchain:

- **highlight.js** — CSS rules targeting `.hljs-*` classes (see this site's
  `docs/src/styles/codeHighlight.ts` for a reference mapping)
- **Shiki** — build a theme object from the token values at compile time
- **Prism** — map token groups to Prism's theme format

Override defaults via `createDesignTheme({ tokens: { color: { code: … } } })` or
`colorMode.dark`. Token groups:

| Token                             | Typical use                               |
| --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| `base`                            | Default foreground                        |
| `keyword`                         | Keywords, types                           |
| `title`                           | Titles, class/function names              |
| `attr`                            | Attributes, numbers, operators, variables |
| `string`                          | Strings, regexps                          |
| `builtIn`                         | Built-ins, symbols                        |
| `comment`                         | Comments                                  |
| `name`                            | Tags, pseudo-selectors                    |
| `section`                         | Headings                                  |
| `bullet`                          | List bullets                              |
| `addition` / `additionBackground` | Diff additions                            |
| `deletion` / `deletionBackground` | Diff deletions                            |

See the [Colors](/theming/colors) reference for palette ramps and semantic color
swatches, [Shadows](/theming/shadows) for elevation tokens, and [CSS variables](/theming/css-variables) for the full custom property
catalog. Example theme presets live under `docs/src/themes/`.
